models.name: UserIdentityConflict
models.docComment:
Ledger of identity-rebinding events: every time an existing local user row
is re-pointed at a different Clerk identity, or two identities are merged.

Three code paths can do this today, all keyed on EMAIL alone:
  * tenant-context.middleware self-heal (adopts an email-matched row),
  * clerk-webhook.service (merges when clerkUserId and email rows differ),
  * clerk-provisioning.service (same shape).

Email equality is good evidence that two records are the same PERSON, but it
is not proof that two CLERK IDENTITIES are — a stale local row whose
user.deleted webhook never landed is enough to hand its memberships to a new
identity.

This table is RECORD-ONLY for now, deliberately. Blocking the rebind
requires knowing how often it legitimately fires and on what kind of rows,
and there is no such telemetry today; a naive gate would break the self-heal
path whose entire purpose is preventing lockouts when the Clerk webhook is
slow or undelivered. Populate this, review it, then decide.

Has no tenant_id: the middleware path detects a conflict BEFORE any tenant is
resolved, which is also why these cannot be written to audit_logs (its
tenant_id is NOT NULL).

fields.docComment: 'rebind' | 'merge'

fields.docComment: Where it happened: 'middleware_self_heal' | 'clerk_webhook' | 'clerk_provisioning'

fields.docComment: The Clerk identity the row is being re-pointed AT.

fields.name: existingUserId
fields.docComment: The local user row being re-pointed, and the identity it held before.

fields.name: membershipCount
fields.docComment: Memberships the surviving row held at the time, for after-the-fact review.

models.name: IdentityOutbox
models.docComment:
Durable, retryable record of an identity side effect that MUST eventually
reach Clerk. Written in the SAME transaction as the local state change, then
drained out-of-band by IdentityOutboxWorker.

Exists because de-provisioning was fire-and-forget: removeMember flipped the
local membership to 'removed' and called Clerk's
deleteOrganizationMembership INSIDE the same interactive transaction, then
swallowed any failure. A failed delete left the user in the Clerk org — still
being issued org-bearing tokens — with nothing recording it. A slow delete
blew the 5s transaction budget and rolled the removal back entirely.

Modelled on api-strategy's sp_event_outbox.

fields.name: uei
fields.docComment: Step 2.3 — government identifiers + code arrays for procurement matching.

fields.name: tangoEntityLastSyncedAt
fields.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P19 — MakeGov/Tango entity shadow sync status.
This is the client's OWN sync bookkeeping; the fetched entity DATA lives
in the GLOBAL `tango_resource_snapshot` table (P15), keyed by this same
`uei` — no separate link row. A UEI is already a global, exact 1:1 key,
and `TangoResourceLink` is reserved for linking INTO Capiro's own global
reference tables (federal_contractor et al.), never to a tenant-owned
row like Client — `tango-store.service.ts`'s `assertKnownLocalType`
refuses that on purpose (decision-log D-34).

`tangoEntityLastSyncedAt` is the last SUCCESSFUL sync — "successful"
meaning a definitive provider answer, found OR not_found; both are
evidence, not a failure (tango.errors.ts's own framing for `not_found`).
`tangoEntityLastAttemptAt` is the latest attempt regardless of outcome,
reported independently so a rail failing repeatedly cannot read as
healthy — same distinction this program already draws for source
freshness generally (baseline-contract-v1.json's
`sourceFreshnessSemantics`). `tangoEntityLastError` is redacted, and
cleared (set null) on the next successful attempt.

fields.name: applicantTypes
fields.docComment:
Grants.gov "Eligible Applicants" values this client qualifies as, e.g.
"Small businesses" or "State governments".

LABELS, not the numeric Grants.gov codes — `federal_grant.eligibility`
stores labels (verified live 2026-07-28: 17 distinct label strings across
816 of 866 rows), and District Nexus F3 eligibility compares the two by
string. A client populated with codes would match nothing. The canonical
list is `GRANTS_GOV_APPLICANT_TYPES` in @capiro/shared.

Until this is populated, `computeEligibility` can only return
`needs_review` or `unknown`, never `eligible`. Empty is the honest default:
it says "we do not know", which is true, rather than guessing a type from
the sector and telling a user they can apply for something they cannot.

fields.name: setAsideCertifications
fields.docComment:
DURABLE socioeconomic certifications the company HOLDS. Canonical values are
the six in `set-aside.ts`: 8A, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, EDWOSB, HUBZONE. Empty
means unknown, never ineligible.

This comment previously named SAM's `typeOfSetAside` vocabulary (8AN,
SDVOSBC, HZC, SBA, SBP) as canonical, and the DTO accepted it. That was the
wrong vocabulary for a company profile and admitted two things that are not
certifications: SBA/SBP are general small-business RESTRICTIONS on a
solicitation (no firm holds an "SBA certification"), and the 8AN/SDVOSBS/
WOSBSS/EDWOSBSS/HZS family are SOLE-SOURCE notice codes — a competition
method, not a status. Recording either then fed the eligibility check, which
read it back as evidence and reported the client `eligible`.

Legacy rows are migrated by `repair-set-aside-certifications.ts`.

fields.name: ldaClientIds
fields.docComment:

this client resolves to (one id per lobbying-firm relationship — a real

confirmed source='lda' ClientIntelMapping rows; reads join

fields.docComment:
Ethical wall (master plan Phase 1): when true, this client's memory
(clio_memory scope='client', client-linked memory_items, and their
embeddings) is recallable ONLY by users granted a ClientMemoryAccess row.
false (default) = the pre-wall relevance-only behavior, so enabling the
column changes nothing until a wall is explicitly erected per client.
Admins are NOT exempt — a real ethical screen binds seniors too; a
user_admin manages grants (and any self-grant is audit-logged).

models.name: ClientMemoryAccess
models.docComment:
Ethical-wall grant (master plan Phase 1): membership row allowing one user
to recall one walled client's memory. Meaningful only while

Fail-closed by construction: a walled client with zero grants is invisible
to everyone (including admins) until a user_admin grants access via

models.name: ClientTeamMember
models.docComment:
Account team: which of the firm's own users work a given client.

Capiro had only `Client.accountOwnerUserId` — one person — so the client
profile's "Account team" had no backing record at all and the UI honestly
rendered "No roster" with no way to add anyone. A row here is ADDITIONAL
team membership; the owner stays on `Client.accountOwnerUserId` and the API
reads the two together rather than duplicating the owner into this table.

`role` is deliberately free text (e.g. "Lead lobbyist"). No controlled
vocabulary exists for it in this product, and inventing an enum would be
fabricated structure. NULL means "on the team, no stated role" — a real
answer, not missing data.

column's arrival cannot retroactively quarantine historical documents;

themself — may approve; there is no second-reviewer/two-person flow.

Clio proposes a plan + clarifying questions, the user answers, and Clio runs
a multi-round agentic investigation across all internal data tools + the web,
then synthesizes a long, cited report. The final report is persisted as a
ClioArtifact (kind = 'research_report'); this row tracks the lifecycle and
the inputs that produced it so a session can be resumed/audited.

Stored as TEXT in the DB with a CHECK constraint (scope IN
('firm','user_private','client') since G2's 20260713020000). Modeled as
String (not a Prisma enum) so the generated client never casts to a
"ClioMemoryScope" Postgres type — that type was never created, and the
enum decl caused `type "public.ClioMemoryScope" does not exist` (42704)
500s on Clio memory reads. App-level union typing lives in
clio/clio-memory.helpers.ts.

boundary (recalled only in this client's conversations), not per-user
access control — no per-user client ACL exists.

by readers + purged by the daily refresh-memory-graph sweep.

models.name: MeriActionApproval
models.docComment:
MeriV2 write-tool approval record (Workstream B4 — the ApprovalStore's
persistence). When a compliance decision is WARN, the orchestrator's gate
holds the write (ApprovalPendingError) until a human approves THIS exact
action. The action is identified by a stable `fingerprint` (sha256 over
tenant+user+tool+canonicalized input, computed in @capiro/meriv2-core's
computeActionFingerprint) — so an approval can never be replayed against a
mutated action. One approved row per (tenant, user, fingerprint).

POLICY not yet decided (needs Neo): approval TTL (rows never expire today),
WHO may approve (self-approve today; four-eyes would add an approverUserId
distinct from userId), and whether one approval survives a re-run (it does
today — the row persists). These are enforced by the service/endpoint on top
of this table, not by the table shape. Tenant-cascade.

fields.docComment: Clerk subject of the user the approval is scoped to (matches MeriContext.userId).

fields.docComment: sha256 hex from meriv2-core computeActionFingerprint (opaque to apps/api).

fields.name: tool
fields.docComment: The write tool this approval authorizes (for display/audit; not part of the key).

models.name: MeriPendingAction
models.docComment:
The exact proposed action behind a WARN decision (fix for the "approving
never runs the write" bug): the compliance gate's `ApprovalPendingError` is
caught at the SAME moment the fingerprint above is computed, and the tool
name + exact input are captured here, keyed by that same fingerprint.

Without this, "approve" only recorded a `MeriActionApproval` row, then the
UI re-ran the turn by resending the user's ORIGINAL prompt for the model to
re-answer from scratch (`mode: 'regenerate'`) — the model re-derives a
fresh, byte-different payload every time (re-researches, rewords), so its
new proposal hashes to a DIFFERENT fingerprint that was never approved, and
the write WARNs again. Forever. (Confirmed live: `update_client_profile` was
approved 8 times over a week and never executed once.)

The fix: on approval, look up the row by fingerprint and execute the tool
DIRECTLY with the cached input — no model round-trip, so nothing can drift.
`consumedAt` makes execution idempotent (approve-once-execute-once) even if
the same fingerprint reappears (a repeat identical proposal) or approve is
double-clicked. Rows are NOT deleted on consumption — kept for audit; a
future TTL sweep is a follow-up, not a correctness requirement (an unclaimed
row is inert, never auto-executes). Tenant-cascade.

fields.name: userId
fields.docComment: Clerk subject of the user this proposal is scoped to (matches MeriContext.userId).

fields.name: fingerprint
fields.docComment:
sha256 hex from meriv2-core computeActionFingerprint — the SAME value the
paired MeriActionApproval row is keyed by; this table is the lookup that
turns "fingerprint approved" into "exact action to run".

fields.name: tool
fields.docComment: The write tool this input is for (dispatched via MeriToolsService.execute).

fields.name: input
fields.docComment:
The exact tool-call input the model proposed when it first WARNed —
replayed VERBATIM on approval, never re-derived.

fields.name: consumedAt
fields.docComment:
Set the moment approval successfully claims + executes this row. NULL =
still pending (or never approved). Never re-executed once set.

models.name: MeriActionProposal
models.docComment:
Immutable, server-created MeriV2 action proposal. Browser approval is by the
opaque id only; tool/input/fingerprint/policy/tenant/user are server authority.

models.name: ClioScheduledTask
models.docComment:
Clio self-scheduled recurring task (W3). A user asks Clio to run something on
a cadence (e.g. a weekly research brief). The runner (scripts/run-clio-scheduled-tasks.ts)
executes due rows through the Clio tool engine with the task's tool allow-list.
Scope mirrors ClioMemory ('firm' shared | 'user_private' owner-only). Tenant-cascade.

fields.name: scope
fields.docComment: 'firm' | 'user_private' (TEXT + app-level union, same rationale as ClioMemory).

fields.name: prompt
fields.docComment: The instruction Clio runs each tick (a natural-language prompt).

fields.name: intervalMinutes
fields.docComment: Cadence in minutes between runs (>=60 enforced at the tool layer).

fields.name: toolAllowList
fields.docComment:
JSON array of tool names this task is allowed to call. Defaults to read-only
research tools; side-effecting tools require explicit opt-in + confirm.

models.name: ClioMcpServer
models.docComment:
Tenant-configured MCP server (F6a). Bearer tokens for streamable-HTTP
servers are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest (same pattern as
IntegrationConnectionToken) and never stored or returned in plaintext.
Tools are bridged as mcp__<name>__<tool>; only allowlisted tools register,
and every bridged tool is treated as side-effecting unless listed in
readOnlyTools.

fields.name: transport
fields.docComment: http (streamable HTTP) | stdio (ops-managed local child process)

fields.name: scope
fields.docComment:
Connector library (connector-library v1):

  ownerUserId). Personal connections act as the person who authorized them
  and are private to that user. ownerUserId is NULL for firm-wide rows.

fields.name: authType
fields.docComment:
'none' | 'token' (static bearer) | 'oauth' (OAuth 2.1 — credentials live in
ClioMcpOAuthCredential). connectionStatus drives the UI status chip:
'connected' | 'pending' (oauth started, not finished) | 'needs_reauth'

models.name: ClioMcpOAuthCredential
models.docComment:
OAuth 2.1 credentials for an `authType = 'oauth'` ClioMcpServer (1:1).
Split out from the server row so the token/secret material lives in one
tightly-scoped, RLS-isolated table (mirrors integration_connection_token).
All secret fields are AES-256-GCM envelopes (ciphertext/iv/authTag), never
stored or returned in plaintext. clientId + registrationJson are the
non-secret RFC 7591 dynamic-registration result; codeVerifier* is the
transient PKCE verifier (cleared after the code exchange).

fields.name: clientId
fields.docComment: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration (client_id is not secret).

fields.name: accessTokenCiphertext
fields.docComment: OAuth tokens.

fields.name: codeVerifierCiphertext
fields.docComment: Transient PKCE verifier (set on start, cleared after exchange).

fields.name: stateNonce
fields.docComment:
Single-use anti-replay nonce for the signed OAuth `state` (set on start,
atomically cleared when the callback consumes it).

and the ESTIMATED cost (computeAiCostUsd, hand-maintained pricing table).

rather than Capiro's shared key. Metering writes are best-effort — a
failed insert never fails the user's generation.

fields.name: cacheReadTokens
fields.docComment:
Prompt-cache token counters (W3.3): read = cache hit (discounted), creation

fields.docComment:
Outreach prompt-assembly spec that produced this generation ('v1'|'v2'); null

models.name: AiRun
models.docComment:
Agentic Tier-1/Tier-2 run provenance (Phase 1 M5.0, agentic doc §5.1) —
modeled on `ProgramElementIngestRun`'s shape-precedent, but a DISTINCT
table (that model tracks PE-budget ingest-loader rows/quarantine counts;
this tracks one AGENT INVOCATION's full envelope). Every column the
proposal's per-output guardrail list demands (schema, source ids,
evidence, confidence, model + prompt version, run id, tool calls,
validation status, human-review status) as columns, not prose. Written
by every Tier-1/Tier-2 caller BEFORE `ai_usage_events` metering (the two
are siblings, not the same row — `ai_run` is provenance/QA, `ai_usage_events`
is spend). `tenantId = null` marks a tenant-agnostic cached-L1 run (global
row, not RLS-isolated to one tenant); tenant-scoped rows are RLS'd like
`ai_usage_events`.

fields.docComment: Matches `ai_usage_events.workflow`'s vocabulary, e.g. 'legiwatch_alert_enrichment' | 'intel_targeting' | 'intel_rules_comparison' | 'intel_qa_review'.

fields.docComment: Null = tenant-agnostic (cached-generic L1 enrichment); set = a tenant-scoped Tier-2 run.

fields.name: clientId
fields.docComment:
W3.1: the client a tenant-scoped Tier-2 run was FOR (targeting briefs are
per-client — chokepoint.forBill is client-scoped). Null for client-agnostic
runs (L1 enrichment, rules-comparison). Lets the run-intel-workflows
idempotency guard key on (bill, client, tenant), not just (bill, tenant),
so a second client tracking the same bill still gets its own brief.

fields.name: provider

fields.name: inputRefs

fields.name: toolCalls
fields.docComment: The tool-call trace (name + args + result summary) for audit/replay.

fields.docComment:
Per-gate drop counts (W3.1) — how many model-asserted targets each

Makes "dropped and logged" (M5-B) inspectable from the row alone.

models.name: MeriAuditLedger
models.docComment:
Post-hoc grounding-auditor ledger (v3 hallucination plan Wave 5). One row per
audited generation turn: the auditor's verdict + the exact findings, so the
SHADOW-mode findings the auditor logs are also queryable/aggregable for the
lexicon tuning that must precede any per-surface `enforce` flip. Tenant-scoped
+ RLS-isolated like ai_run (own-tenant-or-system), FORCE RLS. Findings live in
`findings_jsonb` (array of { check, severity, span, detail }) so the check set
can evolve without a migration; the scalar columns are what dashboards group by.

'outreach-draft-version' + an OutreachDraftVersion id. NULL for

decided stamps, plus a NAMED reviewer (assignedTo). payload carries what

models.name: AlertGenerationRecord
models.docComment:
Gate I (CG-01) — a server-owned record of what governance decided about ONE
alert-memo/district-brief generation, so filing (saveEdited) can check
durable DB state instead of inferring hold status from banner text or a
meri_audit_ledger row — both of which are ABSENT for an entailment-only
hold when the auditor is off or found nothing (the S1-S4 slip-throughs
I_GOVERNANCE.md §1.4 documents). Modeled on OutreachDraftVersion's audit/
approval columns. Written pessimistically — filingState defaults to
'blocked_pending_review' for a held generation BEFORE the review_request
create is attempted — so a crash between the two writes still leaves a
blocking row; filingState only relaxes to 'draft' once createSystem proves
a real review row exists. Additive-only; RLS per the meri_audit_ledger
template.

fields.docComment:
The alert (intel-api id) this generation was produced from. Not an FK —
alerts are not persisted in apps/api.

fields.name: surface

fields.docComment:
sha256 of the generated markdown at write time. The saveEdited lock keys
on the record's existence + filingState, NOT hash equality (Gate I open
decision #2) — an expected edit must not itself invalidate the lock.

models.name: OutcomeEvent
models.docComment:
G3 — structured advocacy outcomes (blueprint §3.1 stage 5 + §5.2 flywheel).
One row per observed result of the firm's work, loosely linked to its
source (outreach/meeting/artifact/campaign/submission) via source_type +
source_id (the EngagementTask precedent). Funding outcomes SNAPSHOT their

them). RLS per the meri_audit_ledger template.

fields.docComment:
response_received | meeting_scheduled | meeting_held | language_included
| funding_changed | filing_completed | commitment_secured | no_action
| pursuit_won | pursuit_lost | pursuit_passed (P36 — `pursuit_` prefixed
so a procurement outcome can never collide with an advocacy one)
| regulatory_action_published (deterministic regulatory correlation —

fields.docComment:
outreach | meeting | artifact | campaign | submission | manual
| funding_opportunity (P36) | regulatory_document (source_id =

models.name: ContextPacket
models.docComment:
Context Compiler v1 packet trace (G1, blueprint §4.6.4). One row per compiled
steering-context packet: which memory files reached a generation prompt
(`items_jsonb`) and which were deliberately withheld and why
(`exclusions_jsonb`: revoked | superseded | empty | over-budget |
unauthorized). Written FIRE-AND-FORGET by the compiler adapters in apps/api,
the orchestrator (shared Prisma client), and apps/workspace (raw INSERT) —
a trace failure never blocks generation. The `id` is the compiler-minted
packetId (NOT db-defaulted) so the trace row and any downstream reference
(audit ledger, provenance panel) share one identifier. RLS like
meri_audit_ledger (per-command policies, FORCE, no null-tenant path).

fields.name: surface
fields.docComment:
ContextSurface: 'chat' | 'ga-chat' | 'outreach' | 'memo' |
'district-brief' | 'research' | 'workspace-gen'

fields.name: ref
fields.docComment: Surface-local anchor: { conversationId? | draftId? | outreachId? | alertId? }

fields.name: items
fields.docComment: ContextPacketItem[]: { layer, id, type, slug, chars, rationale }

fields.name: exclusions
fields.docComment: ContextExclusion[]: { layer, id, type, slug, reason }

fields.name: packetVersion
fields.docComment:
── Phase 1 §3.a — Evidence Packet v2 ──────────────────────────────────────
`items`/`exclusions` above are RETAINED unchanged: they remain the steering-
memory trace every non-Engagement surface writes fire-and-forget. The fields
below are the Engagement generation trust boundary — written SYNCHRONOUSLY
and fail-CLOSED under ENGAGEMENT_GENERATION_GATEWAY.
1 = legacy steering-only trace. 2 = complete Evidence Packet. New writes
default to 2; the migration pins pre-existing rows to 1.

fields.name: directives
fields.docComment: AuthenticatedDirective[] — the ONLY channel rendered as an instruction.

fields.name: evidence
fields.docComment: EvidenceItem[] — refs + BOUNDED excerpts (never whole threads/documents).

fields.name: sourceFailures
fields.docComment: SourceFailure[] — every source that failed to load, with severity.

fields.name: policy
fields.docComment: The resolved GA policy: { jurisdiction, audienceType, version }.

fields.name: modelPolicy
fields.docComment: Pinned generation identity: { provider, model, promptSpecVersion, … }.

fields.name: packetHash
fields.docComment: sha256 over the canonical, stable-key-ordered packet JSON.

fields.name: effectiveTenantId
fields.docComment:
── ContextPacket v2 metadata (20260729010000_memory_governance_context_v2) ──
`packetVersion` above is shared with (and owned by) the engagement gateway
migration; everything here is new. Bodies are never copied into this table.

effectiveTenantId is NOT NULL with NO default (the migration backfills it
from tenant_id then does ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL), so it is REQUIRED
here — every writer must supply it explicitly.

SQL-ONLY (not expressible in Prisma — see the migration):
  CHECK context_packet_version_check (packet_version IN (1, 2))
  CHECK context_packet_budget_check (non-negative, used <= budget)
  PARTIAL INDEX context_packet_v2_trace_idx
    (tenant_id, trace_id, created_at DESC) WHERE packet_version = 2
  PARTIAL INDEX context_packet_v2_surface_idx
    (tenant_id, surface, client_id, created_at DESC) WHERE packet_version = 2

treatment ContextPacket reference (frozen historical evidence).

Async outreach job (plan W4 / §3.3). One row per generate-or-send request the

One recipient's unit of work within an OutreachJob. Claimed atomically

models.docComment:
Engagement Phase 0 — one logical draft "slot" for an outreach record: an
individual recipient, one member of a list, or a whole group that shares one
email. Identified by the wizard's GenerationTargetKey so a regenerate of the
same slot adds a VERSION instead of a second artifact. The row is also the
FOR UPDATE lock target that serializes concurrent version creation.
Owner-private: reads are scoped by tenant RLS *and* the owning user.

fields.name: generationKey
fields.docComment: individual:<recipientKey> | list:<audienceId>:<recipientKey> | group:<audienceId>

fields.name: audienceKind
fields.docComment: 'individual' | 'group'

models.name: OutreachDraftVersion
models.docComment:
Engagement Phase 0 — the IMMUTABLE audited artifact. subject/body/contentHash
are written once and never updated: an edit, AI improvement, regenerate or
revert creates a NEW version pointing back via sourceVersionId. Only the
audit/approval lifecycle columns are mutable, and an approval may never
change content. Every real external delivery references one of these rows.
Statuses are Strings (not Prisma enums) on purpose so a future status can
ship without a PostgreSQL enum migration — see outreach-draft.types.ts for
the authoritative literal unions and the sendability policy.

fields.docComment: The version this one was edited/improved/reverted FROM; null for a fresh generation.

fields.name: contentHash
fields.docComment: sha256 of subject+body — what the audit verdict and any approval attach to.

fields.docComment: 'generated' | 'manually_authored' | 'generation_failed'

fields.name: auditStatus
fields.docComment: 'not_required' | 'pending' | 'passed' | 'warning' | 'held' | 'unavailable'

fields.name: approvalStatus
fields.docComment: 'not_required' | 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'

fields.docComment: The AuditorMode this verdict ran under ('shadow' | 'annotate' | 'enforce').

fields.name: auditDecision
fields.docComment: runAuditor decision, or 'audit_unavailable' when a control itself failed.

fields.name: auditLedger
fields.docComment: The structured auditor ledger entries this exact text was judged against.

models.name: OutreachSendIntent
models.docComment:
Engagement Phase 0 — the DURABLE send intent. Committed, with all of its
delivery rows, BEFORE any provider request is made, so an unrecorded external
send is structurally impossible. Accepts draft VERSION ids only, never raw
caller subject/body. Idempotent per (tenant, user, requestKey): a retried
POST returns the existing intent and sends nothing again.

fields.name: requestKey
fields.docComment: Client idempotency token, minted once per Send click.

fields.name: requestFingerprint
fields.docComment:
Remediation plan §3.c5/c6 — sha256 over the canonical request payload
(tenant, user, parent record, mailbox, sorted version ids, sorted
attachment manifest, signature choice, test mode). Lets a REUSED
requestKey be told apart from a genuine retry: same key + same
fingerprint dedupes, same key + a different fingerprint is refused
(OUTREACH_REQUEST_KEY_REUSED) instead of silently returning the old
intent for a materially different request. Historical rows backfill to
`legacy:<id>`, a format a real `sha256:`-prefixed fingerprint can never
collide with.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: queued | running | partial | complete | failed | canceled

fields.name: totals
fields.docComment: { total, pending, sending, sent, failed, unknown, skipped, held }

models.name: OutreachDelivery
models.docComment:
Engagement Phase 0 — one logical send unit (one recipient, or one whole group
sharing a single email). AT-MOST-ONCE: the row is claimed pending → sending
in an atomic conditional UPDATE before the provider call, and an ambiguous
outcome becomes 'unknown', which is NEVER automatically returned to pending
or retried. renderedSubject/renderedBody are the exact text handed to the
provider, captured at intent creation so a later signature or body edit
cannot mutate an in-flight send.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.docComment:
sha256(tenant + connection + version + envelope + attachment manifest):
the same exact delivery can never be created twice, under ANY request key.

fields.name: provider
fields.docComment: 'microsoft_graph' | 'gmail'

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: pending | sending | sent | failed | unknown | skipped | held

models.docComment:
Per-tenant AI provider key, AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest with
AI_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (same envelope pattern as

fields.docComment:

models.name: ProcurementLine
models.docComment:
── Canonical PROCUREMENT budget line items (P-1 lines / BLINs) ──────────────

A procurement line item (e.g. Procurement, Defense-Wide 0300D / P-1 Line 68 /
0204WARSYS "Warrior Systems <$5M") is NEVER a Program Element (extractors/types.ts
identity guardrail), so it cannot live in program_element*. These three tables are
the procurement analogue of ProgramElement / ProgramElementYear /
ProgramElementSource, written ONLY by ProcurementLineWriterService
(src/defense-budget/procurement/) from composer output whose verification
decision is PASS, and ONLY when DEFENSE_BUDGET_PROCUREMENT_CANONICAL_WRITES=1.
Global tables (no tenant_id / RLS): public-domain J-book data, read-only via API.

Identity: (appropriation_code, line_item_number). The appropriation account code
(0300D, 2031A, ...) already encodes the component, and BLINs are unique within an
account. P-1 line NUMBERS shift from cycle to cycle, so p1_line_number on the line
is "as of the latest written cycle" and the per-FY value is on the year row.

in UNIQUE constraints and Prisma cannot address a compound unique containing NULL
— either would let a re-run insert a duplicate line-level row and break the
writer's idempotency guarantee.

Money columns are $ MILLIONS. Decimal(18,6) rather than ProgramElementYear's
Decimal(14,2): P-1 values are printed in $K, so an exact $M representation needs
three decimals (FY2027 0204WARSYS request = 511,016 $K = 511.016 $M). This is the
precision ProgramElementYearSourceValue.canonical_value_m already uses.

(PE, asserted FY, delta type, fromRef, toRef) — the engine recomputes it
idempotently from ProgramElementYear / ProgramElementBudgetPosition /
ProgramElementProcurementLine. Latest-wins: a recompute that finds a changed
magnitude stamps `supersededAt` on the prior live row (supersededAt IS NULL)
and inserts a fresh one, so history is preserved without breaking the natural
key. Global table (no tenant_id / RLS): the delta itself is public-domain budget
math; clientRelevance is computed PER-TENANT at read time and is NEVER stored.

deltaType (text, enum-as-text — keep parsers tolerant of new types):
  pb_vs_prior_pb | mark_vs_request | mark_vs_mark | conference_vs_marks |
  enacted_vs_request | new_start | termination | zeroed | transfer_candidate |
  quantity_change | unit_cost_change | outyear_shift | project_level_change

  'request'→'hascMark', or 'pb_fy2026'→'pb_fy2027').

from the PURE scorer (deltas/materiality-scorer.ts); clientRelevance is layered
in at read time, never persisted.

IDENTITY vs PROVENANCE (repaired design — see community-funding.identity.ts and
community-funding.upsert.service.ts for the full rationale). This row represents
the GOVERNMENT FUNDING REQUEST itself, never any one document that publishes it.
`sourceDocumentId`/`sourcePage`/`sourceRow`/`sourceHash` used to live directly on
this table and were part of the identity hash — that made the same real request
published in two authoritative documents (e.g. a House subcommittee CPF PDF and
the House consolidated CPF XLSX) become two different canonical rows. Provenance
now lives on CommunityFundingRequestSource (one canonical request, many source
occurrences); the fields below are the canonical, best-known projection of the
request's own attributes, updated per the deterministic precedence rule in
CommunityFundingUpsertService (never overwrite a non-null final/enacted amount
with a requested-only one; prefer a more-advanced amount stage; first-seen wins
on same-stage/same-nullity conflicts — full raw values from every source stay on
the provenance rows regardless of what the canonical projection picks).

models.name: ClientFundingOpportunity
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities — a client's durable WORKFLOW relationship to ONE future
funding opportunity: either a Grants.gov NOFO (`federal_grant`) or a SAM.gov
contract notice (`sam_opportunity`). TENANT-scoped, RLS FORCE-enabled.

── Why this is not ClientGrantNexus ────────────────────────────────────────
ClientGrantNexus answers "does this client have a defensible geographic NEXUS
through federal assistance money" — it is EVIDENCE, and its
'opportunity_candidate' relationshipType was a narrow bolt-on so the District
Nexus opportunity pipeline had something to read. This model answers a
different question: "what is our team DOING about this opportunity". A pursuit
decision is not geographic evidence. Folding the two would let saving an
opportunity start contributing to a district nexus score, which is exactly the
false claim the District Nexus rules forbid — a future opportunity never
creates district context by itself. They stay separate tables on purpose, and
nothing in the District Nexus aggregate reads this one.

Exactly ONE source record is referenced; `source` says which, and a CHECK
constraint in the migration enforces the exclusivity rather than trusting the
writer. No FK to either source table: `federal_grant` and `sam_opportunity`
are GLOBAL upsert-only catalogs, and a hard FK would force cascade semantics
onto tables nothing ever deletes from (same rationale as
ClientGrantNexus.grantOpportunityId / .assistanceAwardId).

fields.name: source
fields.docComment: 'grants_gov' | 'sam_gov'.

fields.name: grantOpportunityId
fields.docComment: FederalGrant.id (a Grants.gov opportunity id) — set iff source='grants_gov'.

fields.name: samOpportunityId
fields.docComment: SamOpportunity.id (uuid) — set iff source='sam_gov'.

fields.name: sourceRecordType
fields.docComment:
GENERIC source identity (P13), alongside — never instead of — the two legacy
pointers above.

The pair of nullable pointer columns works for exactly two sources. Agency
forecasts, DIBBS and SBIR/STTR each want this same durable decision record,
and a third column per source means a wider CHECK, another partial unique
index and another branch in every writer, forever.

`sourceRecordType` is the SHAPE of the thing pointed at
('grants_gov_opportunity' | 'sam_notice' | 'tango_procurement_forecast' | …),
which is a different question from `source` (the product rail) and will stop
being 1:1 with it once Tango supplies three record types under three rails.

NULLABLE for both legacy sources, and that is load-bearing rather than lax:
pre-P13 code writing during a rolling deploy sets neither, so a NOT NULL
would make the older API a hard failure the moment the migration lands.
The migration backfills every existing row; the update path backfills the
rolling-deploy tail; reads fall back to the legacy pointer either way.
A FUTURE source, by contrast, MUST carry both and no legacy pointer — see
client_funding_opportunity_one_source_chk in the P13 migration.

fields.name: workflowStatus
fields.docComment:
'suggested' | 'saved' | 'pursuing' | 'dismissed' | 'won' | 'lost' | 'expired'.
CHECK-constrained in the migration.

fields.name: ownerUserId
fields.docComment:
Assigned owner — `users.id`. Always same-tenant; the service verifies
membership before writing, because a uuid in a request body proves nothing.

fields.name: facilityId
fields.docComment:
Explicit, reviewable project site (`client_facilities.id`). The ONLY path
from an opportunity to a congressional district — never inferred from the
notice, which publishes applicant eligibility (grants) or a place of
performance that may be nowhere near the client (SAM).

fields.name: relevanceScore
fields.docComment:
Deterministic snapshot from when this row was last scored. A SNAPSHOT, not
the live answer: the read path recomputes relevance on every request, so
these exist for producer bookkeeping, alert diffing and audit ("what did we
think when we suggested this"), never as the number rendered to a user.

fields.name: evidenceSourceType
fields.docComment:
How the row came to exist: 'deterministic_relevance_v1' (producer) or
'user_action' (a human saved/pursued it). Mirrors
ClientGrantNexus.evidenceSourceType, and is what lets the producer tell its
own rows apart from a human's.

fields.name: userCreated
fields.docComment: TRUE when a human created this row. The producer must never overwrite one.

fields.name: staleAt
fields.docComment:
Stamped when the producer decides a suggestion IT created no longer clears
the relevance floor. Never applied to a row a human has acted on — a
dismissal or a pursuit is a decision, not a stale guess.

fields.name: sourceStatusSnapshot
fields.docComment: Source lifecycle snapshots used by the deterministic alert/expiry pass.

fields.name: sourceFingerprint
fields.docComment:
Hash of the SOURCE-PUBLISHED content at the last observation, from
`source-lifecycle.ts`. Answers "was this amended" WITHOUT consulting any
local clock: `sam_opportunity.updatedAt` is a Prisma @updatedAt column and
`federal_grant.detailSyncedAt`/`syncedAt` move whenever a job visits the
row, so keying amendment alerts on them alerted on our own syncs. NULL =
no baseline yet, which the processor establishes SILENTLY.

fields.name: sourceActiveSnapshot
fields.docComment:
Whether the SOURCE considered this live at the last observation. Stored
rather than reconstructed from `sourceStatusSnapshot`: a legacy row with no
snapshot reconstructed to "active", so an already-closed opportunity fired
a spurious closure alert the first time it was seen, and a status string
cannot express the date half of the lifecycle at all.

fields.name: humanDecision
fields.docComment:
The team's DECISION, kept separate from `workflowStatus` (where a pursuit is)
and from the machine recommendation (which is recomputed on read, never
stored). A team can decide to monitor something with no pursuit, or to pass on
something whose source is still wide open — folding those into workflowStatus
makes "we chose not to bid" indistinguishable from "the source closed", and
only one of those is a decision somebody can be asked about later.
NULL means nobody has decided yet, correct for every producer-created row.
CHECK-constrained to pursue|monitor|pass (migration 20260819010000), and the
same migration CHECKs that a decision always carries its actor and timestamp.

fields.name: nextAction
fields.docComment:
What happens next, and by when. A due date with no action is a reminder about
nothing, so the migration CHECKs that direction; an action with no due date is
fine.

fields.name: outcomeNote
fields.docComment: Free-text won/lost context. Only ever set by an explicit user action.

fields.name: pipelineStage
fields.docComment:
The pursuit pipeline stage (P35): reviewing | qualified | pursuing |
submitted | won | lost | passed. CHECK-constrained in migration
20260901010000.

A SECOND field beside `workflowStatus`, never a replacement. That column
carries two values that are not capture stages at all — `suggested` is the
producer's own output and `expired` is a mechanical consequence of the
source closing — and it has no room for `qualified` or `submitted`.

NULLABLE, and the NULL is load-bearing twice over. During a rolling deploy
an older pod INSERTs without it and must succeed. And a producer-created
`suggested` row genuinely HAS no stage: mapping it to `reviewing` would put
the producer's whole backlog on a board column named for a human activity
nobody is performing. `expired` is unstaged for the same reason in reverse —
which stage a row was in when the source closed is not recorded, and picking
one fabricates a capture history.

Reads reconcile this with `workflowStatus` in exactly one place
(`effectiveStage` in funding-opportunity-pipeline.ts): the legacy status wins
for anything it can express, and this column only adds resolution the legacy
one cannot.

fields.name: pipelineStageVersion
fields.docComment:
Optimistic-concurrency token. The transition service puts this in the WHERE,
so two simultaneous drags cannot both succeed — the loser updates 0 rows and
gets a conflict rather than silently discarding the other person's decision.
NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 so an older pod's INSERT still produces a usable token.

fields.name: pipelineStageByUserId
fields.docComment:
Who moved it. NULL on a non-NULL stage is MEANINGFUL, not missing: it means
the migration inferred the stage from the legacy status, so the read reports
the basis as derived rather than claiming a person moved it.

models.name: OpportunityBookmark
models.docComment:
A bookmark is independent from client workflow. A NULL clientId is the
tenant workspace scope; partial unique indexes enforce its nullable key.

models.name: TangoResourceSnapshot
models.docComment:
One OBSERVATION of a Tango resource, at a point in time.

APPEND-ONLY AND IMMUTABLE once written: `contentSha256`, `normalizedJsonb`,
`sourceUpdatedAt` and `providerFetchedAt` on a given row never change after
INSERT. The only fields that ever transition are `active` (true → false,
exactly once, when a NEWER observation supersedes this one) and
`supersededAt`. That is the "versioned head" the plan's acceptance criterion
asks for: `(resourceType, externalId)` has at most one row with `active =
true` at any moment — its current head — and every prior observation stays in
the table, unmodified, as history.

DUPLICATE SUPPRESSION: `TangoStoreService.writeSnapshot` computes a canonical
SHA-256 over the normalized payload (stable key ordering, so field-order
noise from the provider never produces a spurious "change") and looks it up
against `(resourceType, externalId, contentSha256)` BEFORE writing anything.
An exact repeat is a true no-op — no row touched, no timestamp bumped — which
is what makes a nightly re-sync of unchanged data free of write amplification.

fields.name: resourceType
fields.docComment:
'entity' | 'opportunity' | 'notice' | 'forecast' | 'vehicle' |
'vehicle_awardee'. Mirrors TANGO_RESOURCE_TYPES in
apps/api/src/external/tango/tango.types.ts (P14) — CHECK-constrained in the
migration to that exact vocabulary, not re-derived from it, since a schema
file cannot import a TypeScript const array.

fields.name: externalId
fields.docComment:
The provider's own identifier for this record (a UEI, an opportunity id, a
forecast id, a vehicle uuid, …). Together with `resourceType` this is the
NATURAL KEY the plan asks for — deterministic, and never Capiro-assigned.

fields.name: schemaVersion
fields.docComment:
Which version of Capiro's OWN mapping (apps/api/src/external/tango/
tango.mappers.ts) produced `normalizedJsonb`. Lets a later phase identify
"this observation was normalized by an older mapper" and re-fetch, even when
the provider's raw content has not changed — a mapper bug fix is not a
provider content change, and conflating the two would hide the fix from
every already-synced row.

fields.name: sourceUpdatedAt
fields.docComment:
The provider's own last-modified stamp for this record, when it supplies
one. NULL is a fact some resources carry honestly — P14's TangoForecast, for
instance, has no modified stamp at all — never backfilled with `fetchedAt`.

fields.name: providerFetchedAt
fields.docComment:
When CAPIRO fetched this observation. Always set; this is "when we looked",
distinct from `sourceUpdatedAt`'s "when the source says it changed".

fields.name: sourceUrl
fields.docComment:
The provider's own URL for this record, when one exists (an opportunity's
`sam_url`, for example). NULL for resource types the provider gives no
direct link for — an entity has none.

fields.name: contentSha256
fields.docComment:
Lower-case hex SHA-256 (64 chars), over a CANONICALIZED serialization of
`normalizedJsonb` (recursively sorted object keys, so key-order noise from
the provider can never look like a content change). CHECK-constrained to the
hex-64 shape in the migration.

fields.name: normalizedJsonb
fields.docComment:
The NORMALIZED domain object (TangoEntity, TangoOpportunity, …) as produced
by tango.mappers.ts — never the provider's raw response. This is what makes
"no raw payload reaches a tenant API" true by construction rather than by
convention: nothing in this column ever held an un-mapped field, because the
mapper's allow-list already dropped it before this row was built.

fields.name: active
fields.docComment:
TRUE for exactly one row per (resourceType, externalId) — the current head.
Enforced by a partial unique index, not just application logic.

fields.name: version
fields.docComment:
Monotonic per (resourceType, externalId), starting at 1. Lets a reader ask
"how many times has this changed" without counting rows by hand.

fields.name: supersededAt
fields.docComment: Set once, when a NEWER observation supersedes this row. NULL while active.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoResourceLink
models.docComment:
A REVIEWED crosswalk between a GLOBAL Capiro resource and a Tango resource.

Deliberately narrow in what it may link. `localResourceType` is
CHECK-constrained to the small set of EXISTING global reference tables
(`sam_opportunity`, `federal_grant`, `federal_contractor`, `federal_award`) —
the exact tables this schema already treats as tenant-scope-exempt. A
TENANT-owned resource (a client, a client_funding_opportunity row) is never a
valid target here: linking tenant data into a globally-readable crosswalk
table would be the same class of leak RLS exists to prevent, just via a table
that has none. Tenant-facing review workflows (a client's entity match, an
enrichment proposal) belong to P19/P20's own tenant-scoped tables instead.

fields.name: localResourceType
fields.docComment:
'sam_opportunity' | 'federal_grant' | 'federal_contractor' | 'federal_award'.
CHECK-constrained in the migration. No FK: the target table is polymorphic
(selected by this column), which Postgres cannot express as a single FK
constraint — enforced instead by TangoStoreService validating against
LOCAL_LINK_RESOURCE_TYPES before every write, and proven by a rehearsal
insert that an unsupported type is refused.

fields.name: localResourceId
fields.docComment:
The target row's own primary key, as TEXT regardless of its native type —
`sam_opportunity.id` is a uuid, `federal_grant.id` is a free-form Grants.gov
opportunity number. Text is the only type that holds both honestly.

fields.name: tangoResourceType
fields.docComment:
Mirrors TangoResourceSnapshot.resourceType. CHECK-constrained to the same
TANGO_RESOURCE_TYPES vocabulary.

fields.name: basis
fields.docComment:
HOW this link was established. Only two values, and neither is a fuzzy
name match — the same "never fuzzy-match identity" invariant P02 enforced
for award history applies here:
  'exact_identifier' — an unambiguous identifier equality (an opportunity
                        id, a solicitation number, a UEI). No human judgment
                        was involved in proposing it.
  'reviewed_manual'  — a human explicitly confirmed this specific pair.
CHECK-constrained in the migration.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment:
'active' | 'rejected' | 'superseded'. CHECK-constrained. A rejection is
DURABLE — the CHECK below requires an actor and timestamp whenever status is
'rejected', the same actor+timestamp pairing rule as P07's human-decision
columns, so a rejection can never be silently recreated as an unattributed
row.

fields.name: confidenceBand
fields.docComment:
'high' | 'medium' | 'low'. CHECK-constrained. Always populated — an
'exact_identifier' link is 'high' by construction; a future phase proposing
a less-certain candidate before promotion would use 'medium' or 'low'.

fields.name: conflictState
fields.docComment:
'none' | 'field_conflict' | 'identity_conflict'. CHECK-constrained. Records
that a linked pair disagrees on some field (P27's per-field agreement
tracking) without resolving the disagreement here — resolution is a
source-precedence decision the linking phase owns, per plan §4.2: no source
silently overwrites the other.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoSyncCheckpoint
models.docComment:
Resumable pagination state for ONE provider-side sync walk.

Keyed on (syncVerb, resourceType, filterFingerprint) rather than just
(syncVerb, resourceType): a sync re-run with DIFFERENT filters — a different
fiscal year, a different NAICS — must not resume from a cursor that belongs to
an unrelated filtered walk. `filterFingerprint` is a deterministic hash of the
exact filter object, so the same filters always land on the same checkpoint
and different filters never collide.

This checkpoint is about Tango's OWN pagination (walking its global
forecast/opportunity/vehicle lists), which is not partitioned by tenant
upstream — a separate concern from P03/P04's tenant-and-client keyset walk,
which already has its own resumable-cursor mechanism in
producer-pagination.ts. The two are not the same cursor and must not be
confused.

fields.name: syncVerb
fields.docComment:
The sync script name, e.g. 'sync-tango-client-entities'. Mirrors
`sync_run.source`'s convention.

fields.name: resourceType
fields.docComment: Mirrors TangoResourceSnapshot.resourceType. CHECK-constrained.

fields.name: filterFingerprint
fields.docComment:
Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the canonicalized filter object used for this
walk. CHECK-constrained to the hex-64 shape, same as the snapshot's content
hash.

fields.name: cursor
fields.docComment:
OPAQUE. Pass back to the provider verbatim; never parsed or constructed
client-side — the same rule as the P10 inbox cursor, for the same reason:
the provider's cursor encoding is not part of any contract Capiro owns.

fields.name: windowStart
fields.docComment:
The incremental "changed since" window this walk is covering, when the sync
is windowed rather than a full walk.

fields.name: completeness
fields.docComment:
'in_progress' | 'complete' | 'incomplete'. CHECK-constrained. Mirrors the
COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE vocabulary in producer-pagination.ts (P03/P04) — the
same two words mean the same thing everywhere in this program.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoApiUsage
models.docComment:
One provider API call, for account-level usage accounting.

NEVER carries a request header or a key — there is no column for either, on
purpose, and `TangoStoreService.recordUsage`'s input type has no field that
could hold one. P18 reads this table to answer "how close are we to the
account's rate limit" and "when did we last successfully sync resource X";
this phase only creates the substrate — nothing writes to it yet.

fields.name: callFamily
fields.docComment:
The gateway method that was called (`getEntity`, `listForecasts`, …) —
mirrors TangoError.operation from tango.errors.ts (P14). Called "call
family" per the plan's own wording.

fields.name: timestampBucket
fields.docComment:
Bucketed to the minute, so usage aggregates cheaply without a GROUP BY over
raw timestamps at query time.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment:
'success' or one of TangoErrorKind's 7 values. CHECK-constrained to exactly
that set, so a usage row's status is always one this program already knows
how to reason about.

fields.name: rowCount
fields.docComment:
How many domain rows the call returned. NULL for a get-by-id call, where
"one or none" is not a count worth a column.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoWebhookDelivery
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P46 — one VERIFIED webhook delivery from Tango.

A row means exactly: at `receivedAt`, bytes carrying this `deliveryId`
arrived, their HMAC-SHA256 matched the shared secret, and `payload` is what
they said. It is NOT a statement that anything is true about the world — the
provider's claim that a notice changed is the provider's claim, and P47
decides out of band, dry-run first, whether it means anything.

Rows exist only for deliveries that PASSED verification, which is why there
is no `signatureValid` field: a bad signature yields a 401 and no row, so
the column could only ever hold `true`.

GLOBAL, not tenant-scoped, and deliberately carries no RLS — a webhook
arrives with no session and no tenant, and this receiver is mounted outside
TenantContext middleware. Inventing a tenant would write a guess into a
durable record. Tenant fan-out is P48's, after P47 resolves a delivery to
real local rows.

fields.name: deliveryId
fields.docComment:
The provider's own delivery identifier. THE idempotency key: a provider
retry hits the unique index and is answered 200 without a second enqueue.

fields.name: eventType
fields.docComment:
Provider vocabulary, stored as stated. Not mapped to a Capiro enum: an
unknown event type must be recordable, since refusing to store an event we
do not yet understand loses the evidence needed to add support for it.

fields.name: eventId
fields.docComment:
The provider's id for the underlying event, when present. Distinct from
`deliveryId` — one event may be delivered more than once.

fields.name: payloadSha256
fields.docComment:
SHA-256 over the exact verified bytes, lowercase hex. A SEPARATE fact from
`deliveryId` and NOT unique: identical content legitimately arrives under
different delivery ids, and holding both lets P47 tell "said the same
thing twice" apart from "said something new".

fields.name: payload
fields.docComment:
Verified bytes, parsed. Stored so P47 can reconcile and replay without
re-asking the provider what it already told us.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment:
Delivery lifecycle only, never outcome: 'received' | 'processed' |
'ignored' | 'failed'. P46 only ever writes 'received'. CHECK-constrained.

fields.name: providerEventAt
fields.docComment:
The provider's own event timestamp, when supplied, used for the replay
window. NULL means the payload carried none — treated as missing evidence,
never as stale evidence.

fields.name: processError
fields.docComment: Sanitized reason a drain failed. Never a secret, never a raw payload.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoEventOutbox
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P48 — one unit of fan-out work.

GLOBAL, like the delivery it comes from: a change in the federal
marketplace carries no tenant. Whether it matters to a client is decided
per-client downstream, against that client's own profile and workflow.

SEPARATE from `TangoWebhookDelivery` on purpose. A delivery is immutable
inbound evidence of what arrived; this carries the MUTABLE work state —
attempts, leases, quarantine — so a poisoned event's retry history never
scribbles on the proof of what the provider actually sent.

Leased rather than locked (`leaseUntil` + `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), so
several processors run without blocking each other and a crashed processor's
row becomes claimable again instead of stuck. Quarantine is TERMINAL and
visible: a row at the attempt ceiling stops retrying and is skipped by the
claim query forever, but it never disappears and never blocks the queue.

fields.name: deliveryId
fields.docComment:
The verified delivery this work came from. No relation, deliberately —
the record that work was queued must outlive what it pointed at.

fields.name: eventIndex
fields.docComment:
Position of this event within its delivery, and part of the idempotency
key. A delivery carrying N events enqueues N rows; replaying it collapses
onto exactly those rows.

The first version keyed on `deliveryId` alone, which made a multi-event
batch UNREPRESENTABLE: the receiver accepted the batch and the outbox kept
only `events[0]`, marking the row done while every later event was
silently discarded.

fields.name: resourceType
fields.docComment:
Which provider resource to refresh. `externalId` is nullable: a payload
may name an event with no addressable resource, and such a row completes
as a no-op rather than retrying forever.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: 'pending' | 'processing' | 'done' | 'quarantined'. CHECK-constrained.

fields.name: lastError
fields.docComment: Sanitized. Never a payload body, never a secret.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoEventAlert
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P48 — one material change, for one client, told once.

TENANT-SCOPED with RLS ENABLED and FORCED, and it carries `tenantId` so
`PrismaService`'s tenant-scope extension picks it up automatically.

── Deduplication is a UNIQUE INDEX, not application logic ──────────────────

Replay and out-of-order delivery are NORMAL for an at-least-once webhook
sender, and P48's acceptance requires they "produce one result". Two
processors racing the same change both reach the INSERT; only the database
can collapse that correctly under concurrency.

The fingerprint is computed from the CHANGE (dimension + before + after),
never from the delivery — so the same deadline slip re-delivered under a new
delivery id collapses onto one alert. This is exactly why P46 stores
`payloadSha256` separately from `deliveryId`.

── No model creates a row here ─────────────────────────────────────────────

`evidenceJsonb` holds the P28 classifier's own before/after values. An LLM
summary may be attached downstream, but it can never bring an alert into
existence — the plan is explicit that model summaries "cannot create the
alert".

fields.name: sourceType
fields.docComment:
Generic source identity (P13), so forecasts and future sources reuse this
table rather than growing a second one.

fields.name: changeDimension
fields.docComment:
P28's vocabulary, reused rather than re-derived. This phase applies policy
to the classifier's band; it does not invent a second severity scale.

fields.name: changeFingerprint
fields.docComment: Lowercase hex SHA-256 over the change. CHECK-constrained to that shape.

fields.name: pipelineStageAtAlert
fields.docComment:
What the row looked like when the alert fired, so a reader can tell why
they were told. A later stage change never rewrites this.

fields.name: sourceObservedAt
fields.docComment:
When Capiro last saw the source. Stale evidence must say so rather than
reading as current.

models.name: ClientProfileEnrichmentCandidate
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P20 — client profile enrichment review workflow.

ONE proposed change to ONE field on ONE client's profile, sourced from
Tango entity data (P19's snapshot), pending human review. TENANT-scoped
(unlike every other Tango-owned model above) because this is fundamentally
about a client's own profile, not a global marketplace fact — see the
migration's own header for why this is a new table rather than
`TangoResourceLink` (reserved for GLOBAL reference tables, never a
tenant-owned row) or `ClientIntelMapping` (a different question: "same
legal entity", not "should this field change").

No `client`/`tenant` Prisma relation object is declared here — matching
`ClientFundingOpportunity`'s own convention (plain scalar
tenantId/clientId, FK enforced in raw SQL, no Prisma-level navigation
needed by anything that reads this table).

fields.name: source
fields.docComment:
'tango' today; CHECK-constrained so a future second enrichment source
cannot silently share this vocabulary without a reviewed migration.

fields.name: field
fields.docComment:
'naicsCodes' | 'pscCodes' | 'setAsideCertifications' | 'cageCode' — the
CLIENT model's own field name, verbatim, not the Tango snapshot's
snake_case. This row is about a client field; a reviewer should not need
a second translation table to know which one.

fields.name: currentValueJsonb
fields.docComment:
The client's value AT PROPOSAL TIME — a snapshot, not a live read, so a
reviewer sees exactly what would change even after the client's live
value has since moved on.

fields.name: contentHash
fields.docComment:
Canonicalized hash of (source, field, proposedValueJsonb) — see
tango-store.service.ts's computeContentHash for the same canonicalization
this reuses. The unique index below is keyed on this, not the raw JSONB,
because Postgres cannot uniquely index an unbounded JSONB value directly.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment:
'pending' | 'accepted' | 'rejected'. A REJECTED row is NEVER resurrected
by a later proposal of the identical content — same durability
principle as tango_resource_link (P15) and client_intel_mapping (P05).
There is no bulk-accept anything: every row is reviewed by its own
primary key, one at a time (this phase's acceptance bar — "no accept-all
for certifications" — generalized here to no accept-all at all).

models.name: ClientRelevantVehicle
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P22 — relevant vehicles and past-performance sync.

A MATERIALIZED, tenant-scoped summary: "this client (or its parent
entity) is an awardee on this Tango vehicle, with this past-performance
summary." The authoritative, versioned observation stays in the GLOBAL
`tango_resource_snapshot` table (P15) — this table exists so a fast,
indexed read never scans JSONB across every vehicle-awardee snapshot
government-wide to answer "which vehicles matter to THIS client". See
the migration's own header for the full reasoning, including why
`relationship` ('self' | 'parent') is never collapsed into one boolean —
`TangoVehicleAwardee`'s own doc (P14) already draws that line, and P23
depends on it staying drawn.

fields.name: tangoVehicleId
fields.docComment:
Matches tango_resource_snapshot.externalId for resourceType='vehicle'.
Deliberately FK-less — global provider data, tenant-scoped summary.

fields.name: relationship
fields.docComment: 'self' | 'parent'. CHECK-constrained in the migration.

models.name: TangoProcurementForecast
models.docComment:
Agency procurement forecast (Funding Opportunities P24) — a pre-
solicitation signal, never an active competition.

GLOBAL, no tenant_id, no RLS — provider catalog data, the same category
as sam_opportunity/federal_grant (P00) and tango_resource_snapshot (P15),
never a tenant- or client-owned fact.

A SINGLE CURRENT-STATE TABLE, deliberately NOT layered on P15's versioned
tango_resource_snapshot the way P19/P20/P22's syncs are. That mechanism
exists to keep a full audit trail of every observed value for a LOW-
volume, per-client-relevant resource; a forecast is a HIGH-volume
(24,000+ live rows, confirmed) catalog record Capiro tracks the CURRENT
state of, the same shape of resource sam_opportunity/federal_grant
already are as single current-state tables. `snapshot` below holds the
full normalized shape of the MOST RECENT observation for audit/debugging
— an upsert overwrites it, it does not grow a new row.

fields.name: tangoForecastId
fields.docComment: Tango's own forecast id. The sync's upsert key.

fields.name: agency
fields.docComment:
The provider's own flat agency label (e.g. "VA") — distinct from, and
not always consistent with, the organization hierarchy below (P24
finding, decision-log D-45).

fields.name: departmentCode
fields.docComment:
Organization hierarchy. Every level independently nullable — the
provider's own hierarchy is not always fully populated.

fields.name: organizationId
fields.docComment: Opaque, stable provider id for the organization node. Never parsed.

fields.name: estimatedPeriod
fields.docComment: Free text, e.g. "Q3 FY27". Not a date, and never parsed into one.

fields.name: pscCode
fields.docComment:
ALWAYS NULL today. Confirmed absent from this resource's own
available_fields (decision-log D-45) — kept for a future provider
release, not an oversight.

fields.name: contractVehicle
fields.docComment:
Free text naming a vehicle, e.g. "To Be Determined". No separate
structured link exists on this resource (D-45) — "vehicle text/link" in
the plan is one field in practice, not two.

fields.name: placeOfPerformance
fields.docComment: Free text, not a structured address — matches TangoForecast's own field.

fields.name: primaryContactName
fields.docComment:
Structured on the live server (D-45) — flattened to columns here since
this table has no JSON contact field of its own.

fields.name: sourceUrl
fields.docComment: ALWAYS NULL today. Confirmed absent (decision-log D-45).

fields.name: providerModifiedAt
fields.docComment:
The provider's own last-touched stamp (D-45) — drives the incremental
sync's modified_after window. Null when the provider never stated one.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.docComment:
Full normalized shape of the most recent observation. Overwritten on
every sync, not versioned — see this model's own doc for why.

models.scopeEvidence: non-standard scope-like field organizationId; needs owner review

models.name: TangoBudgetAccount
models.docComment:
MakeGov/Tango's federal-account x fiscal-year budget rollup (P44).

BETA CONTEXT, NOT CAPIRO'S BUDGET. This table illuminates EXECUTION at the
federal-account grain — what an account was enacted, apportioned, obligated
and outlayed. Capiro's own Program Element tables answer a different
question at a different grain (a line item's request, mark and enacted
amount), and the two must never be compared or merged. Plan §P44 is explicit:
this phase writes no Program Element, project, request, mark, enacted or
canonical defense-budget table, and any relationship between an account and
a PE is a Capiro mapping with its own recorded basis, never a provider
assertion.

GLOBAL — no tenant_id, no RLS. "Federal account 097-0400 obligated $X in
FY26" is a fact about the federal government, same category as
`tango_procurement_forecast`, `sam_opportunity` and `federal_grant`.

SINGLE CURRENT STATE, not layered on P15's versioned snapshot store — the
same deliberate deviation P24 made and recorded as decision-log D-46, for
the same reason: a budget rollup's history is the FISCAL YEAR dimension the
table already carries, so a second versioning axis would store the same fact
twice and invite the two to disagree.

THE MONEY COLUMNS ARE NULLABLE AND NULL IS NOT ZERO. Live observation
(2026-09-01, P44's own shape probe): on a real row `contract_obligated` was
a number while `enacted_ba`, `requested_ba`, `apportioned`,
`obligated_total`, `outlayed_total` and `unobligated_balance` were ALL null.
An account the provider has not attributed is not an account with no money.

fields.name: tangoAccountRowId
fields.docComment: Tango's own row id for this account x fiscal-year pair. The upsert key.

fields.name: federalAccountSymbol
fields.docComment:
Treasury federal account symbol, e.g. "097-0400". The provider's own
identifier for the account, and the ONLY key a Capiro-side mapping may
join on — see this model's doc on why no PE relationship is inferred.

fields.name: agencyCode
fields.docComment: Nullable, and observed NULL on a live row while `agencyName` was present.

fields.name: requestedBa
fields.docComment:
Budget authority and execution. Every one nullable; see the model doc.
`@db.Decimal(20, 2)` rather than a float: these are dollars, and a float
that rounds an obligation is a number nobody can reconcile against the
source.

fields.name: attributionStatus
fields.docComment:
The PROVIDER'S OWN confidence in its attribution, carried verbatim.
This is what makes the "beta" label honest rather than decorative: the
source tells us how sure it is, and the UI repeats it instead of
presenting every row with equal weight.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.docComment:
Full normalized shape of the most recent observation. Overwritten on
every sync, not versioned — same policy as the forecast table above.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoBudgetVendorFlow
models.docComment:
One recipient's contract flow out of one federal account (P44).

RELEVANT VENDORS ONLY. The provider's own recipients endpoint returns every
recipient of an account; this table stores a row only when the recipient's
UEI is one Capiro already knows — the same "walk everything, persist only
what we can defend" discipline P22 applied to vehicle awardees. A table of
every federal recipient would be a copy of USAspending nobody asked for.

GLOBAL, like its parent. The UEI filter decides what gets WRITTEN; it does
not make the resulting row tenant-scoped, because "vendor X received $Y from
account Z" is a public fact and two tenants knowing the same vendor must not
produce two rows.

fields.name: recipientUei
fields.docComment: The join key, and the reason this row exists at all.

fields.name: fundingOrganizationId
fields.docComment:
The funding office, opaque provider id plus its own labels. Nullable
because the provider's recipients rows are not guaranteed to carry one.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (TangoBudgetAccount)

models.name: TangoProcurementProtest
models.docComment:
A bid protest (GAO or the Court of Federal Claims), as the provider states
it (P45).

CONTEXT, NOT A CONCLUSION. A protest on a related procurement is evidence a
capture team should weigh. It is not proof that this procurement is invalid,
that the agency did anything wrong, or that an award will be overturned —
and nothing derived from this table is permitted to say otherwise. The
outcome column holds the provider's own word for what happened and is never
re-phrased into a judgement.

GLOBAL — no tenant_id, no RLS. A GAO docket is a public record about the
federal marketplace, same category as every other tango_* catalog table.

LINKED BY EXACT IDENTIFIER OR NOT AT ALL. `samOpportunityId` is populated
only when the provider states an identifier Capiro can match exactly, under
P27's own one-match rule. A protest about "a similar Navy contract" is not
linked to this notice, because "similar" is not an identifier.

fields.name: tangoCaseId
fields.docComment: The provider's own case id. The sync's upsert key.

fields.name: caseNumber
fields.docComment: The docket number a human reads and can look up, e.g. "B-421234.2".

fields.name: sourceSystem
fields.docComment:
'gao' | 'cofc' as the provider states it. Never normalized into a Capiro
vocabulary — the two forums have different procedures and different
meanings for the same outcome word.

fields.name: outcome
fields.docComment:
The provider's own outcome word, verbatim. Null means the case is open or
the provider has not stated one — NOT that the protest failed.

fields.name: protesterName
fields.docComment:
The protester as named on the docket, plus its resolved UEI when the
provider supplies one. The UEI is the ONLY key a client match may use.

fields.name: docket
fields.docComment:
The docket entries, verbatim. Stored whole rather than flattened: a
docket's shape varies by forum and losing an entry to a column that did
not exist would be losing the record of a filing.

fields.name: samOpportunityId
fields.docComment:
Populated ONLY on an exact identifier match. Nullable forever — most
protests will never link to a notice Capiro holds.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoEntityExclusion
models.docComment:
The provider's exclusion observation for one entity, keyed by UEI (P45).

THERE IS NO EXCLUSIONS ENDPOINT. P17's capability probe established this
against the real account: @makegov/tango-node@1.1.0 exposes no exclusions
resource at all, and the fields live on the Entity record instead
(`exclusion_status_flag`, `exclusion_url`). This table is therefore an
OBSERVATION of an entity's flag at a moment, not a copy of a SAM exclusion
record — and it carries exactly what the Entity resource carries.

WHICH MEANS THERE ARE NO DATES. `exclusionStartDate`/`exclusionEndDate` are
declared and are ALWAYS NULL today: the Entity resource states neither.
They are kept because a future provider release may add them and because the
derivation rule already honours them — not as an oversight, the same posture
P24 took for `psc_code`. Until then, expiry cannot be read off a date, so
FRESHNESS carries that weight: an observation older than the staleness
window is reported `unverified`, never `active`, because "we saw a flag
three months ago" is not "they are excluded today".

ABSENCE IS NOT GOOD STANDING. No row for a UEI means Capiro has not observed
that entity, and a row with the flag clear means the provider did not report
one at that moment. Neither is a clearance, and the read service says so on
every response.

fields.name: uei
fields.docComment: One current observation per entity. The upsert key.

fields.name: exclusionStatusFlag
fields.docComment:
The provider's own flag value, verbatim and untranslated. A boolean here
would throw away the distinction between "the provider said no" and "the
provider said nothing".

fields.name: exclusionStartDate
fields.docComment: Always null today — see the model doc.

fields.name: observedAt
fields.docComment:
When the provider was last asked. This is what expiry is judged on while
no dates exist, so it is NOT NULL.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoDibbsSolicitation
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P40 - DLA bid-board (DIBBS) solicitations.

RFQs and RFP/IFBs in ONE table, discriminated by `documentType`, because
they are the same thing to a pursuer: a DLA bid-board item at line-item
grain, keyed by solicitation + NSN + part number. The provider splits them
across `/api/dibbs/rfqs/` and `/api/dibbs/rfps/` and names two fields
differently for the same concept (`issue_date`/`issued_date`,
`return_by_date`/`closes_date`); those are normalized here, and the source
spelling is recorded in the mapper rather than in a column name.

GLOBAL - no `tenant_id`, no RLS. A DLA solicitation is a fact about the
federal marketplace, not about any one tenant, exactly as
`tango_procurement_forecast` (P24) and `sam_opportunity` (P00) already are.

AWARDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS TABLE - see `TangoDibbsAward`.

fields.name: tangoDibbsId
fields.docComment:
The provider's own row `uuid`. The sync's upsert key, and what keeps
duplicate line items distinct - two rows sharing a solicitation and NSN
are still two rows if the provider issued two uuids.

fields.name: documentType
fields.docComment: 'rfq' | 'rfp'. Bounded by tango_dibbs_solicitation_document_type_chk.

fields.name: solicitationFormatted
fields.docComment: RFQ detail only. The provider's own display spelling - never parsed.

fields.name: purchaseRequest
fields.docComment: RFQ only.

fields.name: nsn
fields.docComment:
Line-item identity. Independently nullable: the provider does not
guarantee an NSN or a part number on every row.

fields.name: quantity
fields.docComment:
RFQ only. Decimal, not Int - the unit of issue can make a quantity
fractional, and the published contract states no type. UNCONFIRMED
against a live response; see dibbs-sbir-rest-contract.md.

fields.name: unitOfIssue
fields.docComment:
RFQ only. The unit `quantity` is counted in. A quantity without its unit
is meaningless, so neither is inferred when the other is absent.

fields.name: setAside
fields.docComment: RFQ only.

fields.name: buyerCode
fields.docComment: RFP only.

fields.name: issuedDate
fields.docComment:
Normalized across the two document types: RFQ states `issue_date` and
`return_by_date`; RFP states `issued_date` and `closes_date`.

fields.name: isOpen
fields.docComment:
The provider's own open/closed judgement. Kept as stated rather than
derived from `closesDate` - a date in the past does not always mean the
provider considers the item closed.

fields.name: techDocsUrl
fields.docComment: RFP only.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoDibbsAward
models.docComment:
Funding Opportunities P40 - DIBBS awards. INFORMATIONAL ONLY.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE TABLE FROM TangoDibbsSolicitation
-------------------------------------------------------------------
P40's acceptance says award rows "are informational and cannot be
pursued". An `isPursuable = false` column would have satisfied that only
for as long as every future query remembered to filter on it. A separate
table makes the requirement structural: an award cannot leak into a
pursuable-opportunity surface through a forgotten predicate, because it is
not in the table those surfaces read.

NEVER SUM total_contract_price
-------------------------------------------------------------------
These rows are LINE-ITEM grain, not contract grain: `delivery_order_number`
and `delivery_order_counter` mean one contract can appear as many rows.
Summing `totalContractPrice` across rows double-counts by construction, and
the published contract defines no safe aggregation, so P40 prohibits one.
If an aggregate is ever needed it needs a documented grain from the
provider first - not a `SUM()` and an assumption.

fields.name: tangoDibbsId
fields.docComment:
The provider's own row `uuid`. Upsert key, and the line-item identity
that keeps two delivery orders of one contract distinct.

fields.name: deliveryOrderCounter
fields.docComment:
The provider's own counter for this delivery order. Part of why these
rows must never be summed - see the model doc above.

fields.name: solicitation
fields.docComment:
The solicitation this award came from, as stated. No FK to
tango_dibbs_solicitation: an award can reference a solicitation Capiro
never synced, and a missing parent must not drop the award.

fields.name: totalContractPrice
fields.docComment:
Money. Decimal, never a float. `totalContractPriceText` is the
provider's own rendering, kept verbatim because it is the only evidence
of what the source displayed when the numeric field is null.

fields.name: awardeeCage
fields.docComment:
The awardee, flattened from the provider's nested
`awardee(uei, cage_code, legal_business_name)`. `awardeeCage` is the
award's own top-level field and is NOT assumed equal to the nested
`awardeeCageCode` - the contract documents both, so both are stored.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoSbirSolicitation
models.docComment:
One SBIR/STTR solicitation CYCLE (P42) - the announcement a topic sits in.

`program` is what separates SBIR from STTR; it is a stored discriminator
rather than two tables, because every other field means the same thing for
both and the provider serves them from one endpoint.

Global, no tenant_id, no RLS: a solicitation cycle is a fact about the
federal marketplace, the same reasoning tango_dibbs_solicitation (P40) and
tango_procurement_forecast (P24) already carry.

UNCONFIRMED AGAINST A LIVE RESPONSE. Nothing has ever called /api/sbir/.
Every column is a conservative reading of a published field NAME; types,
null semantics and date formats are not documented. See
dibbs-sbir-rest-contract.md and the migration header.

fields.name: tangoSbirId
fields.docComment:
The provider's own `solicitation_id`. The upsert key.

NOT a uuid, and deliberately not named as one: the contract doc records
that topics key on `topic_id` and solicitations on `solicitation_id`,
neither of which is the `uuid` DIBBS uses. Assuming a shared identity
column across these APIs is the mistake this name exists to prevent.

fields.name: solicitationNumber
fields.docComment:
The cycle's public number, and the ONLY key a topic carries back here.
NOT NULL because a cycle nothing can be joined to is not usable; the
mapper drops such a record rather than storing it unreachable.

fields.name: program
fields.docComment:
'SBIR' | 'STTR' as the provider spells it. NOT constrained by a CHECK:
the contract documents the field, not its value set, and a bounded
vocabulary invented here would reject a real value on first contact.

fields.name: outOfCycle
fields.docComment: The provider's own flag for a cycle outside the normal schedule.

fields.name: solicitationStatus
fields.docComment:
The provider's own lifecycle word, stored as stated. Never rewritten into
"open"/"closed", and never derived from endDate.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoSbirTopic
models.docComment:
One SBIR/STTR TOPIC (P42) - the unit a small business actually responds to.

WHY THERE IS NO FOREIGN KEY TO tango_sbir_solicitation
