-------------------------------------------------------------------
`solicitationNumber` is the stated link to the parent cycle, unenforced -
the same decision, for the same reason, as tango_dibbs_award.solicitation:
a topic can name a cycle this system never synced (different filter,
different window, or simply not fetched yet), and a FK would make a missing
parent silently drop a real topic.

WHAT THE PLAN ASKS FOR THAT THE PROVIDER DOES NOT PUBLISH
-------------------------------------------------------------------
P42's work item names "topic, agency/component, solicitation cycle, phase,
open/close dates, description, source opportunity/grant link, and DSIP
parent". Four of those have NO documented field on either SBIR endpoint:

  - PHASE (I/II/III) - a real SBIR concept, absent from the published field
    list. No column, because a column nothing can populate reads as "we
    have this and it is null" rather than "the source does not state it".
  - DESCRIPTION - not published on the list resource.
  - DSIP PARENT - `officialSolicitationUrl` may point at DSIP, but a URL is
    not a parent key and must not be parsed into one.
  - SOURCE OPPORTUNITY / GRANT LINK - no crosswalk field exists.

Recorded here rather than solved, so the next reader does not add a column
and populate it from something adjacent. That is the
AwardHistoryFacts.contractOffices mistake, which fed an office signal the
awarding sub-tier because it was nearby.

UNCONFIRMED AGAINST A LIVE RESPONSE - see the sibling model.

fields.name: tangoSbirId
fields.docComment:
The provider's own `topic_id`. The upsert key, and NOT the same field
name the sibling table keys on - see TangoSbirSolicitation.tangoSbirId.

fields.name: topicNumber
fields.docComment:
The public topic number, e.g. an "A24-001" style code. Distinct from
`tangoSbirId`: the provider's row id is not the number a human cites.

fields.name: agency
fields.docComment:
The provider's single `agency` field. There is no separate component
field on this resource, so nothing here is split into one.

fields.name: solicitationNumber
fields.docComment: The parent cycle, as STATED. No FK - see the model doc.

fields.name: solicitationStatus
fields.docComment:
The provider's own lifecycle word for the parent solicitation, stored as
stated. A closed topic is still stored - P42's acceptance is that it stays
REFERENCE-ONLY, which is a rule about what may pursue it, not a reason to
drop it.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoOpportunityParity
models.docComment:
Per-FIELD agreement between Capiro's first-party SAM.gov row and
MakeGov/Tango's own observation of the same opportunity (P27).

EVIDENCE, NOT A MERGE. Nothing in this program writes to `sam_opportunity`
from a Tango observation. Plan §4.2: first-party ingestion stays
authoritative for canonical lifecycle fields, a Tango observation may
verify or identify a conflict, the conflict is RECORDED, and no
"last write wins" merge is permitted. `resolution` starts 'unreviewed' and
the local value stays canonical until a human says otherwise.

The LINK itself is not here — it lives in P15's `tango_resource_link`,
whose `basis` column admits only `exact_identifier` | `reviewed_manual`.
A second link table would mean two answers to "is this linked".

Global table — no tenant_id, no RLS. "SAM.gov and the provider disagree
about this notice's deadline" is a fact about the federal marketplace,
same category as `sam_opportunity` and `tango_resource_snapshot`.

fields.name: tangoOpportunityId
fields.docComment:
The provider's opportunity id. Also the tango_resource_link /
tango_resource_snapshot external id for the same record.

fields.name: samOpportunityId
fields.docComment:
`sam_opportunity.id`. A SOFT pointer with no FK, matching
tango_resource_link's own local_resource_id: a cascade from either
catalog would delete the evidence that they ever disagreed.

fields.name: field
fields.docComment:
Bounded by tango_opportunity_parity_field_chk. Only lifecycle facts BOTH
catalogs carry — a provider-exclusive field would report as a conflict on
every row and belongs in the snapshot instead.

fields.name: localValue
fields.docComment:
Both sides verbatim, stringified for storage AFTER the typed comparison.
NULL means that side stated nothing — never zero, never false, never "no".

fields.name: agreement
fields.docComment:
'agree' | 'conflict' | 'local_only' | 'provider_only' | 'both_absent'.
Five values, not two: "they disagree" and "only one of them said
anything" are different findings and only the first needs a human.

fields.name: resolution
fields.docComment:
'unreviewed' | 'local_canonical' | 'accepted_provider' | 'dismissed'.
'local_canonical' is recorded explicitly rather than left implied, so
"nobody has looked" stays distinguishable from "we looked and kept ours".

fields.name: firstObservedAt
fields.docComment:
When this comparison was first seen with its CURRENT outcome, and when it
was last confirmed. A conflict standing for three weeks reads differently
from one that appeared this morning.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TangoOpportunityNotice
models.docComment:
One observation of one notice in an opportunity's history (P28).

The material-change TIMELINE is DERIVED from these rows at read time by
`opportunity-change-classifier.ts`, never stored: a derived timeline kept
alongside its own inputs is a second thing that can be wrong about them.

Not folded into P15's `tango_resource_snapshot` because the access pattern
is the opposite one — "every notice under THIS opportunity, in order" —
which a (resource_type, external_id) snapshot table cannot answer without
scanning its JSON. Hence real columns for the ordering keys and the compared
facts, plus `snapshot` for the full normalized observation.

Global table — no tenant_id, no RLS. "This solicitation's deadline moved on
14 July" is a fact about the federal marketplace.

fields.name: tangoNoticeId
fields.docComment: The provider's own notice id. The sync's upsert key.

fields.name: tangoOpportunityId
fields.docComment:
The parent opportunity, when the sync knows it. Nullable: a notice can be
observed through a solicitation-number query before its parent is walked.

fields.name: samOpportunityId
fields.docComment:
`sam_opportunity.id` when P27's crosswalk resolved the parent. Soft
pointer, no FK — the history must outlive either catalog's row lifecycle.

fields.name: description
fields.docComment:
The notice body, verbatim. Untrusted source text — never an instruction.
Stored so a later phase has it without re-fetching; nothing on the
timeline path selects it.

fields.name: descriptionSha256
fields.docComment:
SHA-256 of the normalized body. The classifier compares THIS, never the
bodies: a description runs to tens of kilobytes and the timeline query
fetches up to 500 notices. Null when the provider stated no description —
and null on every row written before the field was requested at all,
which is why both columns are nullable rather than backfilled.

fields.name: postedDate
fields.docComment:
The ordering keys. `providerUpdatedAt` is the tiebreaker, so two notices
posted the same day still order deterministically.

fields.name: responseDeadline
fields.docComment:
The compared facts, as real columns: the change classifier reads every one
of them on every timeline request.

fields.name: contentHash
fields.docComment:
Canonical SHA-256 over the normalized observation. A re-sync with
identical content is a no-op — same hash, no new observation, and
therefore no material change in the derived timeline.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: OpportunityAttachment
models.docComment:
An attachment on a federal solicitation, and — once fetched — where the
archived copy lives (P29).

Metadata and archive are ONE row with an explicit `status`, not two tables:
knowing an attachment exists and holding a copy of it are different facts,
and two tables would let them disagree about the same file. Only
`status = 'archived'` may be cited by a downstream claim (P30/P31), and the
database enforces that an archived row carries its bucket, key, byte count
and hash — a failed fetch cannot mark metadata complete.

`refused` and `failed` are separate: one is Capiro declining to go somewhere
(no retry) and the other is a transient condition (retry later).

`archiveKey` embeds the content hash, so identical bytes re-archive to the
identical key and CHANGED bytes get a different one rather than overwriting.
A requirement extracted from version A must still resolve to version A's
bytes after the agency posts version B.

Global table — no tenant_id, no RLS.

fields.name: samOpportunityId
fields.docComment: At least one parent is required (CHECK). Soft pointers, no FKs.

fields.name: sourceUrl
fields.docComment: Verbatim. The natural key together with its parent.

fields.name: fileName
fields.docComment:
Source-stated. All nullable — SAM.gov's resource links routinely carry a
URL and nothing else, and deriving a filename from the last path segment
is a guess that reads like a fact.

fields.name: observedMimeType
fields.docComment: Observed on fetch. Null until then.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: 'metadata_only' | 'archived' | 'refused' | 'failed'.

fields.name: failureReason
fields.docComment:
Bounded machine reason, plus a sanitized detail that NEVER contains any
part of the file body.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: OpportunityDocumentText
models.docComment:
The text of an archived attachment, with its own availability story (P30).

Separate from the attachment row because "we hold the document" and "we hold
its text" are different facts with different reasons for being false. Blank
must never read as "this document has no requirements", so the reason is a
column: `not_entitled` is a billing fact, `not_provided` is a fact about the
document (a scanned fax has no text layer), `pending` and `failed` are
operational.

`attachmentContentSha256` is the binding that makes a citation safe. P31
cites this text as evidence; if the agency reposts the document it archives
under a NEW hash (P29's key IS the hash), this row stops matching, and the
citation reads as stale rather than silently pointing at text that does not
contain the quoted claim.

Provider and local-parser text are never mixed: `extractionMethod` is part
of the uniqueness key, so the two coexist as separate labelled rows.

Global table — no tenant_id, no RLS.

fields.name: attachmentId
fields.docComment: `opportunity_attachment.id`. Soft pointer, no FK.

fields.name: attachmentContentSha256
fields.docComment:
The hash of the exact bytes this text came from. NOT NULL: text with no
binding is text nothing may cite.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: 'available' | 'not_entitled' | 'not_provided' | 'pending' | 'failed'.

fields.name: extractionMethod
fields.docComment: 'provider' | 'local_parser'. Never mixed within a row.

fields.name: providerTier
fields.docComment:
The plan the extraction was made under, so a later downgrade explains
itself.

fields.name: text
fields.docComment: UNTRUSTED SOURCE CONTENT. Never interpreted as an instruction anywhere.

fields.name: truncated
fields.docComment:
True when the provider returned a bounded excerpt. A truncated body that
claimed to be complete would let P31 conclude a requirement is absent from
a document it only half read.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: OpportunityRequirement
models.docComment:
A CANDIDATE requirement extracted from a solicitation document, bound to the
exact bytes and character range it came from (P31).

GLOBAL, because "this solicitation requires a facility clearance at
paragraph 3.2" is a fact about a public document — the same fact for every
tenant, extracted once. The tenant's DECISION about it lives in
`OpportunityRequirementReview`, which is tenant-scoped with RLS.

Every evidence column is NOT NULL. An assertion with no citation is what
this phase exists to make impossible, and a nullable column is a promise the
schema does not keep. The span is checked for coherence and the excerpt's
length must MATCH it — an excerpt longer than its claimed range is a
paraphrase wearing a citation.

`attachmentContentSha256` is the same binding P30's text rows carry: when an
agency reposts a document it archives under a new hash, and every candidate
bound to the old one is stale by construction rather than by a cleanup job.

`extractionMethod` and `extractionModel` are NOT NULL, so "the machine said
so" and "a human confirmed it" can never be conflated on a read.

fields.name: samOpportunityId
fields.docComment:
Denormalized so the detail surface reads a solicitation's requirements
without joining through attachments.

fields.name: requirementType
fields.docComment: Bounded by CHECK. See REQUIREMENT_TYPES.

fields.name: statement
fields.docComment: One sentence, in Capiro's words, of what the excerpt requires.

fields.name: sourceExcerpt
fields.docComment: THE EVIDENCE. All NOT NULL.

fields.name: sourcePage
fields.docComment: Genuinely optional: a plain-text extraction has offsets and no pages.

fields.name: extractionMethod
fields.docComment: 'model' | 'deterministic_pattern' | 'human', and the model/rule id.

fields.name: confidence
fields.docComment: Evidence quality. NEVER a probability that the requirement is real.

fields.name: supersededAt
fields.docComment: Set when a later sync observed the document change under this candidate.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: OpportunityRequirementReview
models.docComment:
One team's decision about one extracted requirement (P31).

TENANT-SCOPED with RLS ENABLED + FORCED and the standard four policies. The
requirement itself is a global fact about a public document; the review is a
fact about one team, and putting it on the shared row would show every
tenant what one team decided.

`reviewedBy`/`reviewedAt` are all-or-nothing with `status`, the same shape as
P07's decision-actor CHECK: a decision nobody can be attributed to is a
decision nobody can be asked about later.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'rejected'.

models.name: FundingOpportunityStageTransition
models.docComment:
One recorded stage move on a tracked opportunity (Funding Opportunities P35).

TENANT-SCOPED with RLS ENABLED + FORCED, unlike the provider catalog tables in
this program: "who moved this to lost, when, and why" is a fact about ONE team.

`actorUserId` is NOT NULL. There is no way to record a stage move nobody
performed, which is what "producers cannot alter stage" means at the schema
level rather than as a convention.

The migration CHECKs that `submitted`, `won`, `lost` and `passed` carry a
non-empty `reason` — a recorded loss nobody explained is a loss nobody can
learn from — and that `fromStage <> toStage`, because a move to where it
already was is not a move.

fields.name: fromStage
fields.docComment: NULL means "entered the pipeline". A real and common first entry.

models.name: ProgramElementAcquisitionProgram
models.docComment:
Reviewed, EXPLICIT map from a DoD Major Defense Acquisition Program (MDAP)
code — as it appears on USAspending contract records
(latest_transaction_contract_data.dod_acquisition_program) — to a Program
Element. This is the defensible bridge that lets the PE contractor panel show
"who are the primes on this program" without inferring PE from coarse funding
accounts. Entries are curated/seeded (not machine-derived), so attribution is
auditable: e.g. ('198','F-35') -> the F-35-related PEs the program tracks.
A program maps to one-or-more PEs and a PE may be reached by one-or-more
program codes; the (acqProgramCode, peCode) pair is unique. Global table —
no tenant_id, no RLS (federal reference data, same as federal_award).

fields.name: acqProgramCode
fields.docComment: MDAP code exactly as USAspending emits it (e.g. '198', '516', 'SDN').

fields.name: acqProgramName
fields.docComment: Human-readable program name for display/provenance (e.g. 'F-35').

fields.name: source
fields.docComment: Where this mapping came from (e.g. 'seed_curated_v1') for auditing.

fields.name: confidence
fields.docComment: 0..1 reviewer confidence; the read path can threshold on this if needed.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: ProgramElementPerformer
models.docComment:
Named prime contractor ("performing activity") for a Program Element, extracted
verbatim from the Service RDT&E Justification Book R-3 "Product Development" /
"Support" / "Management Services" cost-analysis tables (and embedded R-2A tables).
This is the zero-inference, government-STATED PE -> prime link: the exhibit names
the company, contract method/type, performing location, and total contract cost.
Each row carries page-level provenance so the contractor panel can deep-link to
the exact exhibit page ("per the Navy's own FY27 R-3 exhibit, page N"). Global
table (no tenant_id / RLS): J-book data is public-domain reference data, same as
program_element / federal_award. Loaded by the sync-jbook-performers verb from a
committed offline extraction artifact (scripts/__data__/jbook_performers_*.json);
no PDF/Python at runtime. Idempotent: unique on the natural performer key.

fields.name: performer
fields.docComment: Company name exactly as printed in the exhibit (e.g. 'LOCKHEED MARTIN CORPORATION').

fields.name: performerNormalized
fields.docComment: Uppercased/punctuation-stripped name for joins/dedup (e.g. 'LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP').

fields.name: location
fields.docComment:
Performing location as printed (state code 'AL', 'Various', city, or country).
NOT NULL ('' when absent) so the natural-key unique index is deterministic
(Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, which would break idempotent upserts).

fields.name: contractMethod
fields.docComment: Contract method & type token ('SS/IDIQ','C/CPAF','MIPR',...). '' when blank/Various.

fields.name: costCategory
fields.docComment: Cost-category item label from the exhibit row (e.g. 'THAAD Development - Capability').

fields.name: totalCostM
fields.docComment: Total contract cost in $M as printed (TotalCost column). Null when not stated.

fields.name: tableType
fields.docComment: R-3 table family this came from: 'product_development' | 'support' | 'management_services'.

fields.name: projectCode
fields.docComment: Project (R-2A) code/name when the table is under a specific project, else null.

fields.name: publisher
fields.docComment: Publishing component for provenance label (e.g. 'DoD Comptroller (Navy)').

fields.name: isNamedCompany
fields.docComment:
True when the performer is a real named company (has a legal suffix / not 'Various'/
'TBD'/government-internal MIPR). Lets the read path surface only real primes by default.

fields.name: sourceDocumentId
fields.docComment: Registry link (Step 0.1): the fingerprinted source file this performer row came from.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (ProgramElement, SourceDocument)

models.name: Program
models.docComment:
Canonical defense program (e.g. 'F-35', 'SSN 774'). One row per real-world
program-of-record. Seeded from program_element_acquisition_program MDAP codes
(seed-programs.ts) and grown by the matcher / human review. PE links live on
PeProgramMatch, not here.

fields.name: mdapCode
fields.docComment:
MDAP code from the program_element_acquisition_program seed (e.g. '198'); null
for programs introduced outside the curated MDAP map.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: ProgramAlias
models.docComment:
Alias / known name for a Program — drives fuzzy PE/project -> program matching.
aliasNormalized is the upper-cased, punctuation-stripped form used for the
pg_trgm trigram index. aliasType records WHERE the alias came from so the
matcher can weight official names over usage strings.

fields.name: aliasNormalized
fields.docComment: Upper-cased, punctuation-stripped form (see normalizeAlias in pe-program-matcher).

fields.name: aliasType
fields.docComment:
'canonical' | 'acronym' | 'pe_title' | 'project_title' | 'p1_line_name' |
'mdap_name' | 'office_usage' | 'congressional' | 'sam_usage' | 'award_usage'.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (Program)

models.name: PeProgramMatch
models.docComment:
PE (and optionally a project within it) -> Program link, with evidence and a
confidence tier. The graph's source of truth. Machine matches land here as
'candidate'/'quarantined' for HUMAN review; 'accepted' is reserved for curated
seed rows and reviewer confirmations (and the documented official+exact
auto-accept rule). NEVER auto-accepted from a fuzzy path.

fields.name: projectCode
fields.docComment:
Project (R-2A) code within the PE when the match is project-level, else null.
Phase 4 WS M: widened to VarChar(32) to match program_element_project.project_code.

fields.name: evidenceTier
fields.docComment:
'exact_pe_number' | 'exact_project_title' | 'r2a_office_named' |
'other_funding_link' | 'official_office_page' | 'sar_msar' | 'sam_match' |
'award_match' | 'press_release' | 'news_only' | 'mdap_curated' (seed).

fields.name: evidence
fields.docComment: Array of evidence items: { kind, sourceUrl, pageNumber?, quote? }.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment:
'accepted' | 'candidate' | 'quarantined' | 'rejected'. Default derived from
score+tier per the plan thresholds (see deriveMatchStatus).

fields.name: weakSignal
fields.docComment: True when score < 0.50 — stored as a weak signal, NEVER surfaced.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (Program)

models.name: SamOpportunity
models.docComment:
A SAM.gov contract opportunity (solicitation / notice). One row per notice_id.
Loaded by sync-sam-opportunities (DoD-filtered, incremental). Global table —
no tenant_id, no RLS (federal reference data, same as federal_award).

fields.name: noticeId
fields.docComment: SAM.gov noticeId — stable idempotency key.

fields.name: noticeType
fields.docComment:
SAM.gov notice type (e.g. 'Solicitation', 'Combined Synopsis/Solicitation',
'Presolicitation', 'Sources Sought', 'Award Notice').

fields.name: baseType
fields.docComment:
SAM.gov `baseType` — the notice's ORIGINAL type before any amendment.
Distinct from `noticeType`: an amended solicitation carries type
'Solicitation' with baseType 'Presolicitation', and conflating them makes a
sources-sought notice read as an open solicitation. Available on every
search-v2 record; recoverable for already-ingested rows from `raw`.

fields.name: subAgency
fields.docComment:
SAM.gov `subTier` — the service/component beneath the department. Almost
always null on DoD records (the org path is what is populated), so a null
here means "the notice did not say", not "no subagency".

fields.name: setAside
fields.docComment:
SAM.gov `typeOfSetAsideDescription` (human-readable, e.g. 'Total Small
Business Set-Aside (FAR 19.5)'). NULL = full and open, or not stated.

fields.name: setAsideCode
fields.docComment: SAM.gov `typeOfSetAside` (the code, e.g. 'SBA', 'SDVOSBC', '8AN').

fields.name: pscCode
fields.docComment: Product/Service Code.

fields.name: pocName
fields.docComment: Primary point-of-contact name (public header field).

fields.name: active
fields.docComment: Derived from archiveDate: false once the notice's archive date has passed.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: SamOpportunityMatch
models.docComment:
Review-gated SAM.gov opportunity -> Program (and/or PE) link, with a confidence
and a match basis. The graph's source of truth for "which opportunity belongs to
which program". Mirrors PeProgramMatch gating: machine matches land as
'candidate'/'quarantined' for HUMAN review. A verbatim PE-code hit in the
description is the ONLY auto-'accepted' basis; PSC/NAICS-only matches are
'quarantined' and NEVER auto-accepted.

fields.name: matchBasis
fields.docComment: 'program_alias' | 'office' | 'psc_naics_component' | 'description_pe_code'.

fields.name: reviewStatus
fields.docComment:
'candidate' | 'accepted' | 'quarantined' | 'rejected'. Default 'candidate';
only 'description_pe_code' may be 'accepted'.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (SamOpportunity, Program)

models.name: CommitteeReportProvision
models.docComment:
A captured narrative PROVISION from a congressional committee report (HASC/SASC
markup, HAC-D/SAC-D report, conference report) — the LANGUAGE that directs/adds/
cuts/restricts, not just the dollar tables (Step 2.4, plan §4.1 / §6 / §10). GLOBAL
public-domain congressional data (no tenant_id / RLS), like program /
source_document. Populated by the (follow-on) language-extraction loader.

fields.name: committee
fields.docComment: Issuing committee short code: 'HASC' | 'SASC' | 'HAC-D' | 'SAC-D' | 'CONF'.

fields.name: heading
fields.docComment: The provision's heading / item title as it appears in the report.

fields.name: text
fields.docComment: The full provision language (verbatim).

fields.name: actionType
fields.docComment:
Deterministic classifier output (see provision-action-classifier): 'directs_briefing'
| 'directs_report' | 'adds' | 'cuts' | 'transfers' | 'restricts' | 'encourages' |
'expresses_concern'. Null when the language is ambiguous / unclassified.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (SourceDocument)

models.name: ProvisionPeLink
models.docComment:
Review-gated link from a captured committee-report provision to a PE / project /
program. matchBasis records HOW the link was found ('pe_code' from a verbatim PE
number is accepted; fuzzy 'project_title' / 'program_alias' land as 'candidate').
GLOBAL congressional data (no tenant_id / RLS).

fields.name: projectCode
fields.docComment: Phase 4 WS M: widened to VarChar(32) to match program_element_project.project_code.

fields.name: matchBasis
fields.docComment: 'pe_code' | 'project_title' | 'program_alias' | 'manual' — how the link was found.

fields.name: reviewStatus
fields.docComment:
'accepted' | 'candidate' | 'rejected'. Verbatim PE-code links are 'accepted';
fuzzy title/alias links land as 'candidate' for human review.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (CommitteeReportProvision, Program)

models.name: ProgramOffice
models.docComment:
A program/acquisition office (PEO, PM shop, CPE, contracting office, etc.).
People hang off OFFICES and ROLES, never directly off PEs (plan §8/§14). Global
reference data: no tenant_id / RLS, like program / acquisition_personnel.
Time-versioned for reorgs via validFrom/validTo.

fields.name: officeType
fields.docComment: 'peo' | 'pm' | 'cpe' | 'pae' | 'directorate' | 'command' | 'contracting_office' | 'other'

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: PersonRole
models.docComment:
A person's role at an office and/or on a program, with a compliance classification
(contactUse) and review gate. Replaces the free-text person->PE shortcut (plan §8).
Global reference data. staleAt set by the staleness job when observedAt > 180d
without re-assertion (stale roles are excluded from recommendation surfaces).

fields.name: roleType
fields.docComment: 'peo' | 'pm' | 'deputy' | 'chief_engineer' | 'contracting_officer' | 'staff' | 'other'

fields.name: reviewStatus
fields.docComment: 'accepted' | 'candidate' | 'quarantined'

fields.name: contactUse
fields.docComment:
'lobbying_contact' | 'program_ownership_context' | 'official_procurement_poc' |
'internal_owner' | 'relationship_owner' | 'do_not_contact_procurement_sensitive' |
'candidate' | 'quarantined'. Set by the contact-use policy module.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (AcquisitionPersonnel, ProgramOffice, Program)

models.name: ProgramOfficeProgramLink
models.docComment:
Office -> Program link (which office manages/executes/supports a program). Review-gated;
alias-derived links are 'candidate' only. Global reference data.

fields.name: relation
fields.docComment: 'manages' | 'executes' | 'supports'

fields.name: evidence
fields.docComment:
Provenance for derived links (derive-office-program-links). Array of
{ kind, detail, count?, sourceUrl? }. Empty for hand/import-created rows.

fields.name: evidenceTier
fields.docComment:
Highest tier that produced the link: owner_in_office | people_majority |
office_name_exact | por_majority | people_minority | office_name_trgm.

fields.name: matchBasis
fields.docComment: Human-readable basis ("7 of 9 office people map to program X").

fields.name: derivedBy
fields.docComment:
Regenerable cohort tag (e.g. 'derive-office-program-links@v1'); NULL for
hand/import-created links, which the deriver never clobbers.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (ProgramOffice, Program)

models.name: MemoryItem
models.docComment:
Canonical institutional-memory item (plan §0.5). Projected to an Obsidian-
format markdown file in the vault; consumed structurally by the AI /
Intelligence Center. Facts live in the referenced entity row (entityId);
this holds the interpretation/narrative around them. RLS-FORCED on tenant_id.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment:
Phase 1 governance/temporal fields (blueprint Table 19), additive only.
Populated by the candidate write path (1B) and confirm/correct/forget
verbs (1D). Existing rows backfill to status='active', trainingUse=
'excluded', exportable=true (see migration for defaults).

fields.name: confidence
fields.docComment:
Phase 4 — extraction confidence [0,1]; NULL = unscored (human/legacy),
read as the NEUTRAL prior at recall (never demoted). Backfilled from
clio_memory.metadata_jsonb.confidence over the clio: projection linkage.

fields.name: ingestRunId
fields.docComment:
Phase 6 — governed-ingestion provenance. ingestRunId links to the
memory_ingest_run pass that wrote/refreshed this row; reviewState is
'auto' (structural/derived, no review needed), 'unreviewed' (a content
projection awaiting a human confirm in the learned-surface UI), or
'confirmed'. Default 'auto' ⇒ existing rows + recall unchanged.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.docComment:
G2 (20260713020000_memory_client_scope_ephemeral) — ephemeral/working memory.
NULL = durable (every pre-G2 row). The RLS expiry predicate that hides an
expired row ships in 20260713030000_memory_items_expiry_rls.

SQL-ONLY: PARTIAL INDEX memory_items_expiry_idx (tenant_id, expires_at)
  WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL.

fields.name: memoryClass
fields.docComment:
── MeriV2 Phase 3 governance (20260729010000_memory_governance_context_v2) ──
Conservative defaults deliberately carry NO approval and NO authority:
memoryClass/memoryAuthority default to 'legacy_unclassified' (a quarantine
state, never active authority) and governedStatus to 'pending_review'.
Every read/write today goes through $queryRaw; these are modelled so
`prisma migrate dev` cannot propose dropping them.

SQL-ONLY (not expressible in Prisma — see the migration):
  CHECK memory_items_memory_class_check, _authority_check, _scope_check,
    _governed_status_check, _conflict_status_check, _source_excerpt_cap_check,
    _confidence_range_check, _ephemeral_ttl_check, _instruction_authority_check
  PARTIAL INDEX memory_items_review_due_idx (tenant_id, review_due_at)
    WHERE governed_status IN ('active','stale','conflicted')
  PARTIAL INDEX memory_items_conflict_group_idx (tenant_id, conflict_group_id)
    WHERE conflict_group_id IS NOT NULL
  PARTIAL INDEX memory_items_source_identity_idx
    (tenant_id, source_type, source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL

fields.name: controllingItemId
fields.docComment:
Winning row of `conflictGroupId`. Deliberately NO FK in the migration (a
conflict group is resolved by application policy, and a controlling row may
be revoked without cascading), so it stays a bare uuid here too.

fields.name: originContextPacketId
fields.docComment:
context_packet.id this item was extracted from. No FK in the migration —
packets are prunable trace data and must not pin memory rows.

fields.name: duplicateCandidates
fields.docComment: Candidate lineage back-relations (20260729011000_memory_governance_lineage).

fields.name: qualityTelemetryMemoryItemUses
fields.docComment: Phase 27E back-relation — see QualityTelemetryMemoryItemUse.

models.name: MemoryEdge
models.docComment:
Directed graph edge derived from a `[[type:slug]]` wikilink in an item's
markdown (criterion #5). Merged with DB FKs to feed the Intelligence Center
knowledge-graph tab. Re-derived on every save, so it is a cache.

models.name: MemoryCandidate
models.docComment:
Phase 1 (1B) — candidate lifecycle for memory writes (blueprint §4.6.5).
A write NEVER lands in clio_memory/memory_items directly anymore; it
first becomes a candidate row here, which `evaluateMemoryCandidate`
(memory-candidate-rules.ts) resolves to PASS (auto-commit, same
transaction cycle) or WARN (stays 'pending' until an admin approves/
rejects it via memory.controller.ts). `payload_jsonb` carries exactly
what MeriToolsService.saveMemory needs to commit later: key/value/source/
scope/ownerUserId. `committed_memory_id` points at the `clio_memory` row
once committed (clio_memory stays the fast write/recall path per D1;
memory_items remains the write-through governance projection).

fields.name: clientId
fields.docComment: G2: set iff scope='client' — the client the proposed memory belongs to.

fields.name: revisionRootId
fields.docComment:
Phase 2 immutable revision lineage. Prisma owns the database shape,
while lifecycle mutations are restricted to the locked
create_memory_candidate_revision SQL function.

fields.name: confidence
fields.docComment:
Phase 4 — extraction confidence [0,1] for the proposed memory; NULL =
unscored (explicit human save). Drives the model_extraction low-confidence
review rule (memory-candidate-rules.ts).

fields.name: memoryClass
fields.docComment:
── MeriV2 Phase 3 governance (20260729010000_memory_governance_context_v2) ──
The legacy `scope`/`status` columns above are RETAINED untouched for
rollback; `memoryScope`/`governedStatus` are the v2 vocabulary and were
backfilled from them by the migration. governedStatus defaults to
'suggested' (weaker than memory_items' 'pending_review') so a brand-new
candidate is not implicitly queued for review.

SQL-ONLY (not expressible in Prisma — see the migration):
  CHECK memory_candidate_memory_class_check, _authority_check, _scope_check,
    _governed_status_check, _conflict_status_check, _source_excerpt_cap_check,
    _confidence_range_check, _ephemeral_ttl_check
  PARTIAL INDEX memory_candidate_source_identity_idx
    (tenant_id, source_type, source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL
  PARTIAL INDEX memory_candidate_duplicate_item_idx / _contradicts_item_idx /
    _committed_item_idx (tenant_id, <col>) WHERE <col> IS NOT NULL

fields.name: controllingItemId
fields.docComment: No FK in the migration — mirrors memory_items.controlling_item_id.

fields.name: originContextPacketId
fields.docComment: No FK in the migration — mirrors memory_items.origin_context_packet_id.

fields.name: duplicateMemoryItemId
fields.docComment:
── Candidate → item lineage (20260729011000_memory_governance_lineage) ──
Distinct from the legacy `duplicateOfId` (candidate → candidate) and
`contradictsId` / `committedMemoryId` (bare uuids, no FK): these three DO
carry real FKs to memory_items with ON DELETE SET NULL.

fields.name: revisionRoot
attributes: @relation("MemoryCandidateRevisionRoot", fields: [tenantId, revisionRootId], references: [tenantId, id], onDelete: Restrict, onUpdate: NoAction, map: "memory_candidate_revision_root_fk")

fields.name: predecessor
attributes: @relation("MemoryCandidatePredecessor", fields: [tenantId, predecessorCandidateId], references: [tenantId, id], onDelete: Restrict, onUpdate: NoAction, map: "memory_candidate_predecessor_fk")

fields.name: supersededBy
attributes: @relation("MemoryCandidateSupersession", fields: [tenantId, supersededById], references: [tenantId, id], onDelete: Restrict, onUpdate: NoAction, map: "memory_candidate_superseded_by_fk")

fields.name: learningSignalCandidateOutcomes
fields.docComment: Phase 27B back-relation — see LearningSignalCandidateOutcome.

fields.name: qualityTelemetryEvents
fields.docComment: Phase 27E back-relation — see QualityTelemetryEvent.

models.name: MemoryIngestRun
models.docComment:
Phase 6 — governed-ingestion provenance ledger. One row per backfill / cron /
write-through / correction pass into the memory store, capturing actor +
trigger + counts, so every projected memory_items row can be traced to an
auditable pass (memory_items.ingest_run_id). RLS-FORCED on tenant_id.

fields.name: trigger
fields.docComment: cron | manual_backfill | write_through | correction (CHECK-enforced).

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: running | completed | failed (CHECK-enforced).

models.name: MemoryAccessGrant
models.docComment:
MeriV2 Phase 3 (20260729010000_memory_governance_context_v2) — fine-grained
edit/review/approval grant over governed memory. Deliberately NOT an overload
of `client_memory_access`, whose existing meaning is ethical-wall READ
permission. clientId NULL = a firm-wide grant. RLS-FORCED on tenant_id.

SQL-ONLY (not expressible in Prisma — see the migration):
  CHECK memory_access_grant_status_check (status IN ('active','revoked','expired'))
  CHECK memory_access_grant_permissions_check (permissions <@ the 8-verb vocabulary:
    propose, review, approve, edit, confirm, mark_stale, revoke, resolve_conflict)
  PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX memory_access_grant_unique_active
    (tenant_id, client_id, user_id) WHERE status = 'active' — deliberately
    NOT declared as @@unique here: a full unique key would be a lie (it would
    forbid an 'active' grant coexisting with a prior 'revoked' one for the
    same triple) and would expose an unsound findUnique/upsert on the client.

fields.name: grantedByUserId
fields.docComment:
Granter (plain uuid, no FK — mirrors ClientMemoryAccess.grantedBy; survives
the granter's departure).

models.name: MemoryTransitionAudit
models.docComment:
MeriV2 Phase 3 (20260729010000_memory_governance_context_v2) — immutable SOC 2
evidence for governed-memory lifecycle transitions. Ids/status/reason ONLY;
never a memory body. `effectiveTenantId` is the tenant the actor was operating
as (impersonation-aware) and is NOT NULL. memoryItemId / memoryCandidateId
deliberately carry NO FK so audit evidence outlives its subject.

SQL-ONLY (not expressible in Prisma — see the migration):
  CHECK memory_transition_exact_subject_check (exactly one of memory_item_id /
    memory_candidate_id is non-NULL)
  CHECK memory_transition_metadata_size_check (metadata_jsonb <= 32 KiB)

models.name: MemoryCleanupOutbox
models.docComment:
MeriV2 Phase 3 (20260729010000_memory_governance_context_v2) — durable,
idempotent cleanup of SECONDARY projections (clio_memory rows, embeddings,
vault files) after recall has already been suppressed synchronously by the
governed status. memoryItemId / clioMemoryId carry no FK: the outbox row must
survive long enough to delete what the item pointed at.

SQL-ONLY (not expressible in Prisma — see the migrations):
  CHECK memory_cleanup_status_check (status IN ('pending','running','completed','failed'))
  CHECK memory_cleanup_operation_check — widened by
    20260729011000_memory_governance_lineage to: index_memory_item,
    revoke_projections, supersede_projections, expire_projections,
    purge_projections

fields.name: memoryItemId
fields.docComment:
Subject for projection-DELETION jobs. NULLABLE as of
20260811040000_memory_index_outbox_subject: an `index_memory_item` job is
enqueued in the same transaction as the clio_memory write, BEFORE the
memory_items row exists (projectClioMemory is what creates it), so it names
clioMemoryId instead. memory_cleanup_subject_present_check requires that at
least one of the two columns is set.

models.name: LearningSignal
models.docComment:
Phase 27A — Institutional Learning & Quality, signal-capture foundation.
Evidence that Capiro MAY have learned something worth considering for
future reuse, captured directly from existing product behavior (explicit
feedback, accept/reject decisions). Deliberately NOT a second memory
store: no body text is duplicated here, only references to authoritative
source objects (`sourceObjectType`/`sourceObjectId`/`evidenceJsonb`) plus
governance metadata reusing the existing `MemoryClass`/`MemoryAuthority`/
`MemorySensitivity`/`SteeringLayer` vocabularies from `governance.ts` /
`context/contract.ts`. Capturing a row here NEVER writes to
`memory_items`/`memory_candidate`/`clio_memory` and NEVER changes Context
Plane recall — promotion into governed memory is a separate later phase.
See `packages/meriv2-core/src/learning/contract.ts` for the full contract
and `docs/knowledge-plane/phase-27-learning-signal-foundation.md`.

fields.name: actorUserId
fields.docComment:
Always the authenticated actor who performed the action — never a
client-supplied value. Required: every 27A adapter has a human actor.

fields.name: sourceRunId
fields.docComment:
Optional secondary reference (e.g. the fill-with-Meri run a finding
belongs to). Not a lineage FK — same "packets are prunable" reasoning
as `MemoryItem.originContextPacketId`.

fields.name: proposedMemoryLayer
fields.docComment:
Best-guess mapping into the five frozen SteeringLayer values, or null if
this signal isn't a candidate for institutional memory at all. Proposal
only — 27A never acts on it.

fields.name: proposedMemoryClass
fields.docComment: Best-guess MemoryClass, same "proposal only" caveat.

fields.name: evidenceJsonb
fields.docComment:
Array<{type, id}> pointers to authoritative source objects — never a
copy of message/document bodies (see class doc comment).

fields.name: confidence
fields.docComment:
Extraction/observation confidence in [0,1]. NULL means "not scored yet"
— 27A never writes 0 as a stand-in for "unknown" (null != 0 invariant,
same as `durationMs.provider` in Context Plane telemetry).

fields.name: sourceAuthority
fields.docComment:
Subset of MemoryAuthority. Guarded at write time: a human-tier value
here requires `provenanceKind` to be human_explicit/human_implicit —
see `assertNoAiSelfCorroboration` in contract.ts.

fields.name: provenanceJsonb
fields.docComment:
Safe structured metadata only (e.g. originTraceId, originContextPacketId,
model name) — never a raw message/document body.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.docComment: Dedupe key for idempotent capture — see computeLearningSignalIdempotencyKey.

fields.name: observedAt
fields.docComment: When the underlying product event happened (not when it was captured).

fields.name: candidateOutcome
fields.docComment:
Phase 27B — at most one outcome row per signal (unique below); null
means "not yet processed by LearningSignalCandidateService".

fields.name: qualityTelemetryEvents
fields.docComment: Phase 27E back-relation — see QualityTelemetryEvent.

models.name: LearningSignalCandidateOutcome
models.docComment:
Phase 27B — records, for every learning_signal LearningSignalCandidateService
has looked at, whether it produced a memory_candidate and why/why not.
NOT a second candidate store: carries no proposed fact/value, only the
eligibility decision (same relationship memory_transition_audit has to
memory_candidate/memory_items, one layer upstream). Unique per
(tenantId, learningSignalId) — this IS candidate-generation's idempotency
guard for the non-eligible outcomes; the eligible/candidate-created case
is additionally guarded by memory_candidate_learning_signal_source_unique
on MemoryCandidate itself.

fields.name: learningSignalId
fields.docComment:
Single-column unique (not a compound (tenantId, learningSignalId)): a
signal already implies exactly one tenant, and Prisma's one-to-one
relation from LearningSignal.candidateOutcome requires this FK field
itself to be unique.

fields.name: eligibility
fields.docComment:
eligible | insufficient_evidence | negative_feedback_only | duplicate |
unsupported_scope | ai_only | blocked_by_policy

fields.name: memoryCandidateId
fields.docComment: Set only when eligibility = 'eligible'.

models.name: QualityTelemetryEvent
models.docComment:
One row per observed product-quality event. A single generated artifact
typically accumulates several rows over its lifecycle (generated →
edited → approved). Never stores prompt/document/message bodies —
`editMetrics`/`contextLayerCounts` carry only derived numbers.

fields.name: surface
fields.docComment: outreach | workspace | crm_fill | meetings | strategies | meri

fields.name: operation
fields.docComment:
Namespaced operation identifier, e.g. "outreach.draft_version.generate",
"crm_fill.finding.decide". Free text (like LearningSignal.signalType) —
no enum, so new operations never require a migration.

fields.name: eventType
fields.docComment:
Canonical outcome vocabulary (do not add product-specific detail here —
put it in `provenance` instead): generated | edited | regenerated |
approved | rejected | held | superseded | corrected |
feedback_positive | feedback_negative | ignored | unknown

fields.name: artifactType
fields.docComment:
Bare polymorphic pointer to the generated output/artifact this event is
about (an OutreachDraftVersion.id, a Workspace WsDocVersion.id, a CRM
Fill finding id, a MeetingPrep/Debrief.id, a Strategy SpNode/
SpChangeSet id, a ClioMessage.id, ...). No FK: several of these tables
live in other services' databases (Workspace, Strategies), and Prisma
cannot express a polymorphic FK even for the ones that don't — same
reasoning as LearningSignal.sourceObjectType/sourceObjectId.

fields.name: artifactVersionSeq
fields.docComment:
Version/sequence number if the artifact is versioned, purely so a
dashboard query doesn't need a round-trip to the owning service.

fields.name: contextPacketId
fields.docComment:
The Context Plane is centralized in this database regardless of which
service requested it (Workspace/Strategies resolve context through
apps/api's internal ContextPlaneGateway endpoints), so this is a real
FK even for cross-service-originated events. SetNull, not Restrict:
packets are prunable trace data (same reasoning as
MemoryItem.originContextPacketId) and must never pin a telemetry row.

fields.name: contextLayerCounts
fields.docComment:
Snapshot of how many included context items came from each of the five
frozen SteeringLayer values at generation time — counts only, never
item bodies. Shape: { firmIdentity, firmPlaybook, userVoice,
clientSteering, clientPeople }. Null when the surface does not yet
report packet composition (record unknown, never guess).

fields.name: learningSignalId
fields.docComment:
Lifecycle linkage (Phase 27E plan §23): set when this event is known to
trace back to a captured LearningSignal / the candidate it produced.
SetNull — the decision's own audit evidence lives in
memory_transition_audit, not here; this is a convenience join only.

fields.name: editMetrics
fields.docComment:
Safe, numeric-only edit-burden metrics computed ephemerally by the
caller (percentChanged, normalizedEditDistance, versionsCount,
timeToApprovalMs, sectionReplacementCount, ...). Never a diff or body —
enforced by check-quality-telemetry-new-bypasses.mjs.

fields.name: provenance
fields.docComment:
Short safe reason codes / correlation ids only (e.g. { reasonCode,
sampledFrom, computedBy, regenerateOfEventId }) — never free text that
could carry confidential content.

fields.name: traceId
fields.docComment:
Cross-cutting correlation id (ContextPacket.traceId / audit_logs.
request_id) so a full request can be reconstructed across tables
without joining on content.

fields.name: generatedAt
fields.docComment:
When the underlying product event happened (not when this row was
written) — same convention as LearningSignal.observedAt.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.docComment:
Dedupe key — see computeQualityTelemetryIdempotencyKey. Deterministic
from (artifactType, artifactId, eventType, artifactVersionSeq) so
redelivery of the same underlying event never double-counts.

fields.name: evaluationRecords
fields.docComment: Phase 27F back-relation — see EvaluationRecord.

models.name: QualityTelemetryMemoryItemUse
models.docComment:
Join row: "this memory item was included in the packet behind this
telemetry event." Deliberately separate from QualityTelemetryEvent so
per-memory-item usefulness (retrieval count, surfaces used, outcomes
that followed) is answered by aggregating events, never by counters
mutated onto memory_items itself (Phase 27E plan §12).

fields.name: tenantId
fields.docComment:
Denormalized from the parent event so the tenant-scope guard (any model
with a tenant_id column is auto-covered — see tenant-scope-guard.spec.ts)
applies here too, and isolation doesn't depend on always joining
through the parent row.

fields.name: memoryItemId
fields.docComment:
SetNull (not Restrict), matching MemoryCandidate's own FKs to
MemoryItem — a hard-deleted memory row must never block deleting or
reading historical telemetry.

fields.name: contextLayer
fields.docComment:
One of the five frozen SteeringLayer values this item was included
under for this packet.

models.name: EvaluationRecord
models.docComment:
Phase 27F — controlled evaluation of institutional-context effectiveness.

Records ONE shadow comparison for a sampled real request: the same
generation replayed with the five institutional SteeringLayers withheld
(authoritative facts/retrieval/evidence held identical), scored with
deterministic product metrics and, optionally, a blinded model judge.
This is the controlled counterpart to QualityTelemetryEvent's purely
observational "context X present, outcome Y followed" — see
`packages/meriv2-core/src/evaluation/contract.ts`'s module doc comment
for the full invariant list (never mutates production state, never
becomes a LearningSignal/MemoryCandidate, never stores prompt/output
bodies).

Lifecycle: a row is written `pending` or `skipped` synchronously and
never blocks the request it shadows; a detached (fire-and-forget) task
started at generation time — not a later worker reading a persisted
job, because the replay's inputs (evidence/prompt) are ephemeral and
must never be persisted — later transitions the SAME row to
`running`/`completed`/`failed`.

fields.name: clientId
fields.docComment:
Bare scalar, no Prisma relation and no Client back-relation — same
convention as QualityTelemetryEvent.clientId (a bare tenant-scoped
pointer, not a traversable relation the already-large Client model
needs to carry another array for).

fields.name: surface
fields.docComment:
outreach | workspace | crm_fill | meetings | strategies | meri — reuses
QualityTelemetryEvent's exact vocabulary (see the CHECK constraint).

fields.name: operation
fields.docComment:
Namespaced operation identifier, same free-text convention as
QualityTelemetryEvent.operation (e.g. "outreach.draft_version.generate").

fields.name: evaluationType
fields.docComment:
Closed comparison-design vocabulary — one value today
("institutional_context_ablation"); a future per-layer ablation study
is a new value, not a reinterpretation of this one.

fields.name: skipReason
fields.docComment:
Set only when status = 'skipped'. Shares one vocabulary with
'not_sampled' (the sampling-stage skip) so this column never needs a
second CHECK depending on which stage produced the skip.

fields.name: failureReason
fields.docComment:
Set only when status = 'failed'. A short code, never a stack trace or
provider error body.

fields.name: contextPacketId
fields.docComment:
The TREATMENT run's own already-resolved, already-persisted
ContextPacket — frozen historical evidence (§18/§32). Never mutated;
the control arm is an in-memory projection, never written back here or
anywhere else. SetNull: packets are prunable trace data.

fields.name: qualityTelemetryEventId
fields.docComment:
Convenience join to the canonical outcome-truth row for this same
artifact, if Phase 27E already recorded one (§31: "Quality Telemetry
remains source of outcome truth" — this table never duplicates it).

fields.name: treatmentArtifactType
fields.docComment:
Bare polymorphic pointer to the REAL product output being evaluated —
same no-FK reasoning as QualityTelemetryEvent.artifactType/artifactId
(some referenced tables live in other services' databases).

fields.name: treatmentOutputHash
fields.docComment:
sha256 of the treatment/control output text — identity/comparison only,
never the body itself (enforced in application code, not just here).

fields.name: controlProjectionPolicy
fields.docComment:
Which control-projection policy produced the control arm — versioned
independently of configVersion so a future second projection policy
(e.g. a per-layer ablation) is distinguishable from this one.

fields.name: metricsJsonb
fields.docComment:
Deterministic product metrics (§20) — numeric/boolean/enum dimensions
only, e.g. { normalizedEditDistance, structureAdherenceScore,
ctaPresent, findingOverlapRate, ... }. Never a diff or body — enforced
by check-evaluation-new-bypasses.mjs.

fields.name: judgeJsonb
fields.docComment:
Optional blinded model-judge result (§21) — { judgeModel, judgeVersion,
rubricVersion, armOrder, dimensions, inputTokens, outputTokens }. Null
whenever deterministic metrics alone were used (§20: not the default).

fields.name: costJsonb
fields.docComment:
Cost/token accounting for the ONE incremental provider call this
evaluation added (§24). Unknown fields stay null — never coerced to 0.

fields.name: samplingKey
fields.docComment:
The deterministic sampling key (tenantId:operation:artifactId) this
decision was made from — kept for audit/reproducibility, not reused as
the uniqueness key (idempotencyKey below also folds in configVersion).

fields.name: configVersion
fields.docComment:
Bundled eligibility+sampling+projection+metric-rubric version (§29).
Two rows with different configVersion are never assumed comparable.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.docComment:
Dedupe key (§28) — see computeEvaluationIdempotencyKey. A retry of the
same underlying request reaches the same row, never a duplicate.

models.name: Claim

fields.name: artifactId
fields.docComment:
Forward-referenced ids (ClioArtifact / Phase-5 TranscriptSegment); kept as
plain uuid columns (no FK) so this store does not couple to those tables.

models.name: Evidence
models.docComment:
A source citation backing a Claim (Appendix B canonical ids). tenant_id is
denormalized from the parent Claim for RLS defense-in-depth.

models.name: ComplianceCheck
models.docComment:
PASS/WARN/BLOCK record written by the Phase-2 compliance precheck engine —
warehouse #6, the system of record for approval gates.

models.name: BudgetAction
models.docComment:
§1.2 — one normalized committee/appropriations event per (line, fy, stage,
action), derived deterministically from program_element_year marks by
derive-budget-actions. Powers the Movement feed, watchlist signal feed,
catalog Signal chips, and the 360 Legislation tab's action list.
stage: PB|HASC|SASC|HAC_D|SAC_D|CONF|ENACTED (REPROG/SUPP reserved for
report-language/reprogramming ingests that don't exist yet).
action: add|cut|new_start|termination (hold|transfer|rescission reserved).

fields.name: amount
fields.docComment: Signed $ MILLIONS measured against `baseline`; null for non-monetary events.

fields.name: baseline
fields.docComment: What `amount` is measured against: request|prior_stage|prior_year.

fields.name: note
fields.docComment: Render-safe one-liner ("SASC +$42.0M over request").

fields.name: evidenceJson
fields.docComment: §1.4 provenance: the source numbers this action was derived from.

fields.name: billId
fields.docComment:
Bill that asserted this action, when attributable (LEG-B; null until the
marks ingestion carries bill identity — never inferred).

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: BudgetLineRelationship

fields.name: relType
fields.docComment:
related_pe_exhibit|same_program|rdte_to_procurement|procurement_to_om|
predecessor_successor|same_capability

fields.name: evidence
fields.docComment: Human-readable evidence ("P-40 'Related PEs' lists 0604011A").

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: Capability
models.docComment:
§1.6 — curated demand-side capability ("I sell X — where's the money?").
Seeded from scripts/__data__/corrected_json/capabilities_seed.json by
seed-capabilities; grown only by curation, never by unreviewed inference.

fields.name: aliases
fields.docComment: Search aliases ("GPS-denied", "alt-nav", "M-code").

fields.name: taxonomyPath
fields.docComment: Two-level taxonomy path ("Autonomy › Positioning & Timing").

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: CapabilityBudgetLineMatch
models.docComment:
Capability ↔ budget line match with auditable evidence. matchedOn records
exactly which signal produced the match ('title_keyword:PNT',
'description_keyword:counter-UAS', 'curated'), so the finder can always
answer "why is this line recommended?".
models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (Capability)

models.name: ProgramElementIntelligenceCache
models.docComment:
Catalog-sortable engine outputs, refreshed wholesale by
derive-intelligence-cache (delete-and-rewrite). One row per live budget
line. The per-PE intelligence endpoint still computes live; this cache
exists so the CATALOG can filter/sort thousands of lines by maturity /
appropriability / signal without running engines per row per request.

fields.name: lineType
fields.docComment: RDTE_PE|PROCUREMENT_BLIN|OM_BLI (MILCON_PROJECT/TRANSFER/CLASSIFIED reserved).

fields.name: maturity
fields.docComment: Transition-maturity rung 0-5 (F19); null when not applicable/classifiable.

fields.name: maturityJson
fields.docComment: Full ladder: rungs with reached/evidence strings.

fields.name: appropJson
fields.docComment: Factor breakdown incl. unscored factors (F27) — per-factor evidence.

fields.name: signalType
fields.docComment: Latest budget_action on the line: add|cut|new_start|termination|... + tone.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: BillBudgetLineLink
models.docComment:
Bill ↔ budget-line link with typed evidence (legislative-timeline plan
LEG-B; consolidated plan §1.5). Replaces the flat CongressBill.peCodes
array as the system of record for WHY a bill is linked to a line — the
array stays for back-compat/GIN-filtered list queries, this table carries
the evidence. GLOBAL (no tenant_id / RLS), public-domain congressional data.
Mirrors ProvisionPeLink review discipline: only a verbatim PE code in
official bill text is auto-accepted; everything fuzzier lands candidate.

fields.name: linkType
fields.docComment:
explicit_pe_code | budget_table_row | committee_mark_row | report_language
| title_match | manual

fields.name: evidence
fields.docComment: Render-safe evidence ('Found in enrolled bill text: "…0603270A…"').

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: BudgetPackage
models.docComment:
One budget cycle for one domain, e.g. ('defense', 2027) = "FY27 Defense Budget".
Parent of every vehicle and funding position in that cycle.

fields.name: domain
fields.docComment: Budget domain. 'defense' initially; the model is domain-generic on purpose.

fields.name: name
fields.docComment: Display name, e.g. 'FY27 Defense Budget'.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: 'open' | 'enacted' | 'lapsed' | 'closed' — cycle rollup, not a vehicle status.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: BudgetPackageVehicle
models.docComment:
One legislative vehicle inside a package: the presidential request, a chamber
NDAA, a defense-appropriations bill, a conference report, a CR, a supplemental,
or the enacted public law.

A package MAY have MULTIPLE vehicles at the same (track, stage) — a chamber can
move more than one bill, and omnibus/minibus/supplemental vehicles coexist.
Nothing may assume one row per stage forever (§3.2, §5 edge cases 21-22).

fields.name: track
fields.docComment:
@capiro/shared BUDGET_VEHICLE_CLASSES: request | authorization | appropriation
| interim_funding | supplemental | reconciliation.

fields.name: stage
fields.docComment: @capiro/shared FUNDING_STAGES: president | house | senate | conference | enacted.

fields.name: billId
fields.docComment:
Canonical congress_bill id when the vehicle IS a bill. No FK: congress_bill is
loaded by a separate pipeline and a vehicle can be announced before the row lands.

fields.name: reportNumber
fields.docComment: Committee/conference report number, e.g. 'H. Rept. 119-512'.

fields.name: publicLaw
fields.docComment: Public law number once enacted, e.g. 'P.L. 119-86'.

fields.name: label
fields.docComment: Display label, e.g. 'House NDAA (H.R. 8070)'.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: 'introduced' | 'reported' | 'passed' | 'enacted' | 'failed' | 'expired'.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (BudgetPackage, SourceDocument)

models.name: FundingPosition
models.docComment:
One officially-sourced topline dollar figure, in MILLIONS, pinned to a fiscal
year, a pipeline stage, a vehicle class, and an exact funding scope.

HARD RULE (§3.2): a delta may only be computed between two rows with the SAME
fiscalYear AND the SAME scope. Core DoD discretionary, Function 050, total
national defense, and the defense-appropriations title are DIFFERENT scopes and
are never subtracted from one another.

Authorization and appropriation stay SEPARATE rows, never coalesced into one
unlabelled "current" amount (§5 edge case 14).

verificationStatus is the review ladder: parsers write 'extracted' and NEVER
'verified' (§3.3); a human promotes to 'reviewed' then 'verified'; a figure
replaced by a later official number becomes 'superseded' and is KEPT for audit.
Live-row uniqueness is a PARTIAL unique index (excluding 'superseded') created in
the migration, so history accumulates without breaking the natural key.

fields.name: billId
fields.docComment:
Denormalized from the vehicle so Bill 360 resolves positions by bill id in ONE
index hit; kept in sync by the loader.

fields.name: vehicleClass
fields.docComment: @capiro/shared BUDGET_VEHICLE_CLASSES.

fields.name: stage
fields.docComment: @capiro/shared FUNDING_STAGES.

fields.name: scope
fields.docComment: @capiro/shared FUNDING_SCOPES — the measurement basis. NEVER null.

fields.name: amountMillions
fields.docComment: Dollars in MILLIONS. Decimal (not float) so reported figures round-trip exactly.

fields.name: effectiveDate
fields.docComment: When the figure took effect / was published.

fields.name: verificationStatus
fields.docComment: @capiro/shared FUNDING_VERIFICATION_STATUSES: extracted | reviewed | verified | superseded.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (BudgetPackage, BudgetPackageVehicle, SourceDocument)

models.name: BudgetInterimFundingPeriod
models.docComment:
One continuing-resolution / lapse window in a fiscal year's funding history:
the CR sequence, the date it funded through, whether a lapse (shutdown)
followed, and the vehicle/public law that carried it.

Powers the historical CR + shutdown timeline. R3 creates the table and the
loader path; the FY2022-FY2026 backfill and its UI are R4/R7.

fields.name: sequence
fields.docComment: 1-based order within the fiscal year. Gaps are a data error (§3.7).

fields.name: coverageThrough
fields.docComment: The date this vehicle funded operations THROUGH. Must be >= startDate (§3.7).

fields.name: vehicleLabel
fields.docComment: e.g. 'CR #1 (H.R. 5371)' | 'Full-year CR' | 'Consolidated Approps. Act, 2026'.

fields.name: shutdownDays
fields.docComment: Days of lapsed appropriations that began at the end of this period. 0 = no lapse.

models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field; all FK targets are global_reference (SourceDocument)

models.name: CompliancePolicyPack
models.docComment:
A versioned compliance policy pack (packages/meriv2-core/src/assurance/
policy-pack.ts, CompliancePolicyPack) with its full lifecycle recorded.

`packKey` is the stable identity across versions; `version` is the immutable
release. A partial unique index enforces AT MOST ONE `published` version per
(tenant, packKey) in the database rather than in whichever code path publishes
next, and DB CHECKs restate the load-bearing in-code guards: a non-production
pack cannot be published, a published pack must carry review + publication
attribution, and four-eyes requires two DISTINCT reviewers.

`rulesHash` is policyPackRulesHash(pack) — tamper evidence over the
decision-bearing rule material only, so review/publication churn does not
change it but an out-of-band rule edit does.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: draft | pending_review | reviewed | published | retired | disabled_example

fields.name: legalReviewStatus
fields.docComment: not_required_product_policy | pending | approved | rejected

fields.name: authorityJson
fields.docComment: PolicyAuthority — what authorizes this pack to exist at all.

fields.name: fallbackOutcome
fields.docComment: PASS | WARN | BLOCK. Defaults to WARN so an unmatched action fails safe.

fields.name: nonProduction
fields.docComment: Defaults TRUE: a pack is non-production until someone deliberately says so.

models.name: CompliancePolicyPackEvent
models.docComment:
APPEND-ONLY lifecycle ledger for a policy pack: create / submit_review /
review / approve / publish / retire / rollback / simulate. There is no update
path — the row IS the evidence. `metadataJson` is size-capped by a DB CHECK so
this can never become a place to smuggle a payload dump.

fields.name: rolledBackFromPackId
fields.docComment: Set on a rollback: the version rolled back FROM.

models.name: CompliancePolicyDecision
models.docComment:
The SELECTED-VERSION audit: which pack version, and which rule inside it,
bound one specific action. Without this there is no way to answer "what policy
actually applied on that date" once a pack has been republished.

`policyPackId` is NULLABLE on purpose so a no-pack-selected FAIL-SAFE decision
is still recorded rather than silently unlogged, and `binding`
(proposalPolicyBinding: pack@version:rule) survives deletion of the pack row.
`simulated` distinguishes a dry run from an enforcement event.

fields.name: outcome
fields.docComment: PASS | WARN | BLOCK

models.name: AssuranceEvalRun
models.docComment:
One evaluation RUN and its category-specific release decision
(packages/meriv2-core/src/assurance/eval-gate.ts, ReleaseGateReport).

`thresholdsJson` stores the thresholds ACTUALLY USED, so a later threshold
change cannot retroactively rewrite whether a past release was allowed.
`provenanceHash` is unique per tenant, making a re-run of the identical
provenance tuple idempotent instead of duplicating history. The sign-off columns
cover cost/latency ONLY — there is deliberately no generic override column,
because a safety or scope invariant is not waivable.

models.name: AssuranceEvalResult
models.docComment:
One eval CASE outcome within a run. `caseId` is what an accepted feedback
fixture key points at (AssuranceEvalFixture.fixtureKey), so a regression traces
back to the feedback that created its fixture.

fields.name: severity
fields.docComment: critical | high | medium | low

models.name: AssuranceEvalDomainGate
models.docComment:
The per-DOMAIN gate verdict, stored as immutable evidence rather than
re-derived from AssuranceEvalResult later. Re-derivation would silently change
if the summarizer changed; the point is that the per-domain verdict AT RELEASE
TIME is a fact on the record — one critical legislative / tenancy / approval /
compliance regression blocks release regardless of the average.

models.name: AssuranceFeedbackCandidate
models.docComment:
A candidate regression fixture raised from real user feedback, PENDING human
review (packages/meriv2-core/src/assurance/feedback-fixtures.ts).

Feedback never becomes golden truth automatically. DB CHECKs restate the
in-code invariants: a decided candidate must name its reviewer/time/reason, an
ACCEPTED candidate must be anonymized under a named anonymization version, and
the reviewer must not be the creator — you cannot promote your own feedback.

`summary` is reviewer-facing and size-capped. Prompt/response BODIES are
deliberately absent: a fixture references a trace and a claim-ledger hash, it
does not store the conversation. `sourceMessageId` carries no FK so the evidence
outlives a deleted conversation.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: pending_review | accepted | rejected

fields.name: reasonCodes
fields.docComment: Canonical codes only, enforced by a DB CHECK against the apps/api vocabulary.

models.name: AssuranceEvalFixture
models.docComment:
An ACCEPTED regression fixture. `fixtureKey` is the deterministic
'feedback-<sha>' that AssuranceEvalResult.caseId references.

The source candidate is ON DELETE RESTRICT: a fixture must never become
unattributable by deleting its provenance.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Phase 10B-18 Part C — source-bundle member manifest.

`DefenseBudgetExpectedSource` is one identity slot per (fiscalYear,
authorityTrack, sourceFamily, stage, chamber, committee, component); its
dedup key structurally CANNOT distinguish more than one physical document
for that slot (Phase 10B-18 Part B). For source families that really are
one document, that has always been fine. For families the publisher splits
across multiple volumes (Army's FY24 R-2 exhibit is 10 separate BA-volume
PDFs under ONE Army/pb_r2/FY2024 slot), this table is the deterministic
member manifest: one row per REQUIRED-OR-OPTIONAL physical document the
bundle needs, keyed by a stable identity derived from publication structure
(volume/budget-activity), never a physical filename (those are unstable).

A row's `member_status` only ever advances forward (missing -> observed ->
verified) and is the input `evaluateBundleCompletenessV1` (@capiro/
defense-domain) reduces to a single completeness fact. An expected source
with ZERO rows here is the ordinary single-document case and is untouched
by this table — see that function's `no_bundle` outcome.

models.name: DefenseBudgetCycleManifestRegistry
models.docComment:
Phase 10B-2D -- the smallest governed persistence addition this PR makes.

Phase A audit finding: no durable table stored the governed
`BudgetCycleManifestV1` itself -- only its content hash, on
`budget_extraction_candidate_v1.manifest_content_sha256` and the RDT&E/
non-RDT&E cycle bundles' own `manifestContentSha256` field. Every family
certifier needs the manifest's document inventory (required keys, exhibit
mapping, family completeness requirements) to run, and after a process
restart there was no way to reload it -- only the CLI file path the
original operator happened to pass. This is restart-unsafe by
construction: readiness/materialization running in a fresh process has no
access to that file.

This table stores the manifest verbatim, keyed by the same
`manifestContentSha256` every other durable row already carries, so a
governed manifest becomes reloadable by content hash alone. It is
append-only and content-addressed (a manifest is immutable once filed
under its hash); write-once via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.

Preserves the existing schema everywhere else: no other table's shape
changed to make this restart-safe, and every existing consumer of
`manifest_content_sha256` continues to write/read that column exactly as
before.

provenance and artifact back-links referencing the node all survive and

source of that predicate is LIVE_NODE_WHERE (strategy/live-node.ts).
Restoring a NEWER version whose snapshot contains the node revives it
(archivedAt back to null) because snapshot node ids are stable.

fields.name: heartbeatAt
fields.docComment:

is the clock the reconciler measures a state's timeout against (see
run-state.ts RUN_STATE_POLICY) — updatedAt is unusable for that because any
unrelated column write bumps it.

fields.docComment:

the loop-breaker: a run that reconciliation cannot fix stops being retried
automatically and is escalated to a human instead of being swept forever.

fields.docComment:

idempotencyKey (`exec:<nodeId>:<kind>#<attempt>`) — and links back here.

reissue. Plain audit pointers, deliberately NOT Prisma relations: a
replaces/supersedes chain must keep resolving after historical cleanup of
either endpoint, which a required/cascading relation would fight.

already embeds in `summary` as `[watch:<code>:<ids>]` (parsed via
parseWatchMarker) — promoted to a real column so getState can JOIN a
proposal to its source run finding without regex-parsing prose. Null for

fields.docComment: The OLD proposal this row reissues (set on the NEW row).

fields.name: supersededByChangeSetId

must survive that and suppress the SAME watchKey forever (until the user
un-dismisses, which this plan does not add a path for — see the Phase 3
plan's own scope: "Dismiss permanently suppresses").

instead of starting a second generation.
