grouping of terms with a client position + priority. Hearing-style flat terms
keep topicId = NULL (watchlist-global); bill-tracker terms hang off a topic.

models.name: WatchlistMatch
models.docComment:
A match between a transcript segment and a watchlist term — the atomic unit
the alert layer consumes. Carries the score + the segment anchor.

models.name: TrackedBill
models.docComment:
A client's curated tracked bill + the lastSeen snapshot used by shadow change
detection. billId is the raw congress_bill.id string (e.g. "119-hr-1234").

fields.name: position
fields.docComment:
Bill 360 editable client-bill context (Release R1, §1.3). All nullable/
additive; analyst-owned (origin=analyst) — NEVER overwrite canonical bill
status. `note` above is preserved; `analystNote` is the new deliberate home.

fields.name: lastSeenStatus
fields.docComment:
LegiWatch B watermarks — separate signals the action-text watermark can't
see: canonical status transitions (rule_failed/passed_chamber), cosponsor
count deltas (momentum), and text-version changes (updateDateIncludingText).

fields.name: lastSeenFiscalId
fields.docComment:
Last-alerted CBO estimate id / hearing id — gate B7 fiscal + B3 hearing to
fire only on a genuinely new id (else pre-existing rows false-alert on the
2nd sweep and re-fire every 14 days). Baselined on the first B-sweep.

fields.name: lastHearingSessionId
fields.docComment:
Phase 6 (§9.2 step E): Board "discussed at hearing" badge. Set by the
bill-hearing linker; kept SEPARATE from the lastSeenAction* congress watermark
(which detect-bill-changes owns — clobbering it corrupts change detection).

models.name: BillMatch
models.docComment:
Per-(client,bill) recommendation-match snapshot (LegiWatch B1, new_match).
Recommendations were compute-on-read only; this persists which bills have
already crossed a client's watchlist fit floor, so the new-match detector
can anti-join and fire exactly once per newly-matching bill (dedup = the
unique key, not the 14-day window). NOT a tracked bill — a candidate the
client has not yet added to the board.

fields.name: congress
fields.docComment:
Nullable (State Legislation Platform, Phase 0) — congress is meaningless
for a state-bill match row. jurisdiction carries 'US' | <state code>.

models.name: IntelAlert

fields.name: dedupeKey
fields.docComment:
Phase-6 idempotency key (§9.4/§9.5): 'combined:'+clientId+':'+billId+':'+sessionId
or 'hearing:'+clientId+':'+sessionId. Added by the Phase-6 migration; NOT
present in the Phase-3/Phase-4 intel_alert — do NOT assume it before Phase 6.

models.name: IntelAlertPreference
models.docComment: 1:1 carry of the legacy apps/api alert_preference (per user, per client).

fields.name: jurisdictions
fields.docComment:
State Legislation Platform (Phase 0, DD5) — empty = ALL jurisdictions the
client's watchlist produces (today's behavior: state alerts are already
gated by the watchlist opt-in above, so no one gets state spam by default).

models.sensitivityEvidence: fields: emailEnabled, emailAddress, emailCadence, smsPhone, smsPhoneVerified

models.name: IntelNotificationLog
models.docComment:
Send-idempotency log. The unique (alertId, userId, channel) preserves the
legacy §6 idempotency contract — a given alert reaches a user/channel once.

models.name: IntelAlertDigestQueue
models.docComment: Digest queue for daily/weekly cadences (flushDigests target).

models.name: IntelSmsVerification
models.docComment:
One-time SMS phone-verification OTP (hashed). Consent record for the SMS
channel — the verify step is the opt-in (P1.1 port of the legacy apps/api
sms_verification; D2 forbids intel-api writing that table, so the consent
ledger moves here with the service that will deliver SMS post-cutover).

models.name: HearingSmsConsent
models.docComment: Explicit opt-in is scoped to one person, client, purpose and destination.

models.name: IntelWsTicket
models.docComment:
Single-use, short-TTL ticket authorizing exactly ONE WebSocket upgrade to
/intel-api/live.

A browser cannot set an Authorization header on a WebSocket, so the previous
design put the full Clerk JWT in the query string — where it lands in ALB,
proxy and browser logs — then RETAINED it on the connection for up to four
hours and relayed it to MeriV2 long after it had expired. This replaces that
with a credential that is useless after one use and dies in 60 seconds.

The raw ticket is never stored, only its SHA-256. Mirrors the hashed-OTP
shape of IntelSmsVerification above.

tenant_id is TEXT (not @db.Uuid) like every other intel_* table: the RLS
predicate casts current_tenant_id()::text, and a uuid column here would fail
at runtime with PG 42883 "operator does not exist: text = uuid".

fields.name: ticketHash
fields.docComment: SHA-256 hex of the raw ticket.

models.name: IntelFeedback
models.docComment: Feedback labels on alerts/bills/hearings/recommendations (§10 training set).

fields.name: reason
fields.docComment:
§4.10 (Gate E phase f): a structured reason for a marked_irrelevant
dismissal — wrong_issue|wrong_entity|too_broad|already_handled|not_actionable.
Null for every other signal and for a pre-phase-f dismissal (no reason
picker existed yet).

fields.name: matchedTags
fields.docComment:
§4.10 (Gate E phase f): the watchlist topic labels this bill matched AT
DISMISSAL TIME (RecommendationBill.matchedTags, already on the client).
Forward-only — historical rows before this column existed carry `[]` and
contribute nothing to feedbackSignal's aggregation. This is what lets a
dismissal be traced back to the TOPIC that over-matched.

fields.name: matchedTopicIds
fields.docComment:
Gate K (MP-09, c-1): the TOPIC IDS behind matchedTags's topic entries
(never issue areas, which have no topic id). This is the id-keyed twin
of matchedTags — feedbackSignal prefers this and falls back to
matchedTags/label for a row written before this column existed, so a
topic rename no longer severs its accumulated dismissal signal.
Forward-only, same posture as matchedTags itself.

models.name: IntelActionItem
models.docComment:
Actionable-recommendation state on an alert: the memo↔alert link (kind='memo',
carries the apps/api EngagementAttachment id + title so the Feed shows "memo
drafted" and can reopen the Document) plus curation items (kind='talking_point'
with text, kind='report' flag) and the agentic Tier-2 output (kind='targeting_brief',
written cross-realm by apps/api run-intel-workflows, M5.4). memo/report/targeting_brief
are singletons per alert (enforced by a partial unique index in the migration);
talking_point may be many.

models.name: IntelAlertWorkState
models.docComment:
P2-04 (Gate D phase e): PER-USER triage state for an alert.

Deliberately NOT `intel_alert.status`. That column is the shared, firm-wide
state of the intelligence EVENT — read by DEFAULT_STATUSES and written by
dedupeStateActionAlerts and the emitter — so one analyst dismissing an alert
there would hide it from everyone and collide with the suppression sweep.

Work state is an ADDITIONAL narrowing of the feed, never a widening: a
suppressed alert stays excluded regardless of what any user did here.
Keyed on (alertId, userId), which is the idempotency contract — a repeated
action upserts rather than inserting a duplicate. Deliberately NOT keyed on
(clientId, sourceRef, changeType): a recurrence after the 14-day dedup window
is a NEW alert row and should correctly arrive un-dismissed.

fields.name: state
fields.docComment: new | in_review | assigned | actioned | snoozed | dismissed

fields.name: assignedTo
fields.docComment: A user id from the tenant's own team roster. Required when state='assigned'.

models.name: IntelParityRun
models.docComment:
Phase 5 parity audit (§8.6). One row per parity-report run per scope. Compares
what the legacy apps/api tracker DECIDED to fire (durable `intelligence_change`
rows, source='congress_bill' + data.tracker=true) against the shadow
`intel_alert` set over a rolling window. Read-only against both alert sources;
this row is the ONLY write the parity task performs. `git_sha` attributes a
green streak to a specific image.

models.name: LiveHearingSession
models.docComment:
A live (or scheduled/ended) hearing capture session. Tenant-scoped; links to
apps/api-owned records (client, hearing, committee, bill, PE, agency) BY ID
only — no cross-schema FK.

fields.name: publicCaptureId
fields.docComment: Review context for an existing canonical capture; never owns another recorder.

fields.name: sourceUrl
fields.docComment:
Optional source the analyst will PLAY in a browser tab, captured at session
creation so the Live Hearing Room can embed or link it instead of the user
pasting it by hand. Either direct media (HLS .m3u8 / MP3 / AAC / MP4) or a
hearing/event/YouTube reference page — the server never ingests it; the
transcript comes from the tab audio the analyst explicitly shares. NULL =
enter it in the room.

fields.name: consentAttestation
fields.docComment:
Consent attestation audit (P8/D11): for PRIVATE sessions the operator's full
attestation text is a durable compliance artifact — persisted here (not just
logged/truncated), with who attested + when. NULL for public proceedings.

models.name: HearingMediaPermission
models.docComment:
Phase 4 source-specific grants are operator-reviewed capability evidence.
Creating/following a calendar event never creates a grant or capture demand.

models.name: HearingPublication
models.docComment: Unofficial evidence publications. Every edit creates another immutable version.

models.name: TranscriptSegment
models.docComment:
A finalized transcript segment from Deepgram. Client-relevant text is stored
ENCRYPTED (AES-256-GCM, mirroring meeting_debriefs): textCiphertext + iv +
authTag + keyVersion. Non-sensitive public text MAY be stored as textPlain.
NEVER both. Interim (non-final) transcripts are NOT persisted.

fields.name: textCiphertext
fields.docComment: Encrypted text (client-relevant):

fields.name: textPlain
fields.docComment: Plaintext text (non-client-relevant public hearing content only):

models.name: KeyQuote
models.docComment:
A flagged quote worth saving. Points to a transcript segment + timestamp
(satisfies SC5.6). Quote text inherits the segment's encryption posture.

fields.name: textCiphertext
fields.docComment: Encrypted quote text:

models.name: LiveActionItem
models.docComment: An action item / follow-up extracted from a hearing statement.

fields.name: description
fields.docComment: Prose. Null when the session is sensitive — see the encrypted quartet below.

fields.name: textCiphertext
fields.docComment: Encrypted description (same AES-256-GCM scheme as KeyQuote):

models.name: EntityMention
models.docComment:
A policy entity detected in a segment (bill/client/PE/agency/office/company).
entityRef is the canonical id (bill_id, committee_id, UEI, PE id, etc.).

fields.name: entityLabel
fields.docComment:
Prose. Null when the session is sensitive — the label is then in the
encrypted quartet below. Read via HearingBriefService.reveal().

fields.name: textCiphertext
fields.docComment: Encrypted entity label (same AES-256-GCM scheme as KeyQuote):

models.name: LiveSummaryCard
models.docComment: A live summary card pushed to the Live Hearing Room UI.

fields.name: title
fields.docComment:
Prose. Null when the session is sensitive. `cardType` stays plaintext because
the supporters/opponents split matches on it.

fields.name: titleCiphertext
fields.docComment:
TWO independent payloads: title and body are separate prose fields, so one
shared name set cannot hold both.

models.name: OnboardPurchaser
models.docComment:
The person who registers and pays. NOT a platform user unless they
designate themselves a role at the role-designation step (in which case a
Clerk org membership is created for the same Clerk user).

fields.name: tenantId
fields.docComment: Set once provisioning links this purchaser to a tenant.

models.name: OnboardSession
models.docComment:
One resumable funnel run. A purchaser has at most one active (non-failed,
non-provisioned) session; killing the browser mid-funnel resumes at `state`.

fields.name: profiles
fields.docComment: Paid tier: number of client profiles purchased (>= 10). Trial: fixed 10.

fields.name: roleMode
fields.docComment: 'self' (purchaser is the billing admin) | 'invite'.

fields.name: roleDesignations
fields.docComment: [{email, role: 'super'|'admin', firstName?, lastName?}] — designated at 1.7.

fields.name: importMode
fields.docComment: 'self' | 'managed' (Capiro-managed kicks off the CS handoff).

fields.name: orgProfile
fields.docComment: {legalName, vertical, teamSize, timezone, locale, address:{street,city,state,zip}}

fields.name: slugFinal
fields.docComment: Server-generated slug (never user input). Set during provisioning.

fields.name: stripeSetupIntentId
fields.docComment: Stripe SetupIntent id (trial method-on-file) — verified before provisioning.

fields.name: stripeSubscriptionId
fields.docComment: Stripe Subscription id (paid path) — created at the payment step.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.docComment: The tenant this session provisioned. UNIQUE — the idempotency backstop.

models.name: OnboardConsent
models.docComment: One consent record per accepted document (two per signup: tos + sa).

fields.name: signerName
fields.docComment:
── E-signature ceremony (Flow 1.5) ─────────────────────────────────────
Captured when the purchaser types their name/title and signs. Nullable:
consent rows written before the e-sign step predate these columns, and
versions are immutable SOC-2 evidence so old rows are never backfilled.
Signer's typed full legal name (the person who accepted).

fields.name: signerTitle
fields.docComment: Signer's typed job title / role.

fields.name: signatureName
fields.docComment: The exact signature string the signer typed (their "wet-ink" equivalent).

fields.name: signatureMethod
fields.docComment: How the signature was captured — 'typed' today (drawn/uploaded later).

fields.name: envelopeId
fields.docComment:
Shared across the two consent rows (tos + sa) of one signing event, so a
signature can be traced to a single "envelope" like a DocuSign packet.

fields.name: docSha256
fields.docComment:
SHA-256 (hex) of the exact formal-PDF template the signature attests to —
binds the signature to a specific document artifact for integrity.

fields.name: emailCopyRequested
fields.docComment: Whether the signer asked for a copy of the signed PDF to be emailed.

models.name: OnboardLegalDoc
models.docComment:
Versioned legal documents. `planVariant` = 'all' | 'trial' | 'paid' — the
SA text shown is tailored to the plan chosen. Exactly one active row per
(docType, planVariant) is enforced in application code.
models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: OnboardSetupTask
models.docComment: Org-level Flow-2A task state (multi-admin safe; see OnboardTaskKey).

fields.name: detail
fields.docComment: Task-specific payload (e.g. import progress, firm-AI section completion).

models.name: OnboardItInvite
models.docComment:
IT-admin invite. The IT admin has NO Capiro account: the emailed link
carries a single-purpose token (stored hashed) that opens the one-task
connect page. Multiple simultaneous invites per tenant are allowed.

fields.name: provider
fields.docComment: 'microsoft' | 'google' — set when the grant lands.

fields.name: entraTenantId
fields.docComment: Customer Entra tenant id captured from the admin-consent callback.

fields.name: googleWorkspaceDomain
fields.docComment:
Customer Google Workspace primary domain (id_token `hd` claim) captured
from the Google verification callback. Null for consumer-Gmail grants.

models.name: OnboardEmailLog
models.docComment:
Outbound onboarding/lifecycle email log. `dedupeKey` makes every send
idempotent (e.g. "trial_d25:<tenantId>:<periodKey>") so cron double-runs
can never double-send.

models.name: OnboardBillingEvent
models.docComment:
Append-only audit of billing/lifecycle transitions per tenant (SOC 2
evidence + debugging: who/what moved billing_status, slots, locks).

models.name: Tenant

fields.name: onboardingFlowVersion
fields.docComment: Onboarding columns (added by apps/api migration 20260706_onboarding_v1):

models.scopeEvidence: root entity special-case: Tenant is the tenant itself

models.name: User
models.scopeEvidence: root entity special-case: User is the user itself

models.name: Client
models.docComment:
Client profiles (apps/api-owned, RLS'd) — mirrored read-only for slot
counts (billing summary / cap math). onboard-api never writes clients.

models.name: StripeEvent
models.docComment:
Stripe webhook idempotency log (created by apps/api's 20260614120000_billing
migration; onboard-api becomes its only writer).
models.scopeEvidence: no tenant/user/client field and no outgoing FK relations

models.name: TenantUsageMeter
models.docComment:
LLM-overage meter state per tenant per billing period (apps/api-owned
table; onboard-api's overage cron becomes its only writer).

models.name: WsDraft
models.docComment:
A draft = one work product (or packet of documents) produced by the engine.
The full intake config lives in `config` (JSONB, ws-config-v4 shape). Hot
fields are promoted to columns for the Documents library filters.

fields.name: ownerId
fields.docComment:
Owner identity is the Clerk user id (e.g. "user_2abc..."). The engine does
not own the Capiro user table, so it stores the verified Clerk subject
rather than a Capiro user UUID. (Resolved by TenantGuard from the JWT.)

fields.name: lastEditedById
fields.docComment:
Clerk user id of whoever last edited (autosaved) the draft; null for legacy
rows → the UI falls back to the owner. Same id-space as ownerId.

fields.name: industry
fields.docComment: Cascade hot-fields (promoted from config for indexed filtering).

fields.name: isPacket
fields.docComment: Packet derivation (handoff §12.10): isPacket = coverLetter || documents>1.

fields.name: ask
fields.docComment:
Dollar ask (handoff §12.11): { amount, pb, delta } for funding products,
else null. Human-set + lobbyist-gated; never auto-populated.

fields.name: config
fields.docComment:
The full engine config (industry, product, pathways[], committees[],
personalize, officeAssociated, offices[], selectedTemplate, sections[],
pages, tone, linkedData[], anonymize, coverLetter, letterhead, ...).

fields.name: intakes
fields.docComment: Two-step Max draft flow (PR #964).

models.name: WsGuestComment
models.docComment:
A comment left by an unauthenticated guest viewing a public /share/:token link.
Guests carry no identity (no Clerk user, no tenant membership) — the record
exists so the internal team can actually see client-facing feedback; it is
never returned by the public share endpoint itself.

fields.name: body
fields.docComment: Sanitized (HTML-stripped, length-capped) plain text — never raw guest input.

fields.name: guestName
fields.docComment:
Self-reported display label only (e.g. "Jane, Acme Corp") — NOT a verified
identity. Sanitized the same way as body.

models.name: WsCollaborator
models.docComment:
A collaborator on a work product (the WsDraft the user is editing; surfaced in
the UI as "this document"). The draft owner (WsDraft.ownerId) is the implicit
Owner and is NEVER stored as a row — it is synthesized with role "owner" on
read. Every other person/email with access is a WsCollaborator row.

Identity: an INTERNAL teammate carries `subjectId` (their Clerk user id; the
engine doesn't own the user table so it stores the verified Clerk subject,
mirroring WsDraft.ownerId / WsComment.authorId). An EXTERNAL invite carries
`email` only and is `pending` until accepted. Tenant-scoped.

fields.name: subjectId
fields.docComment: Clerk user id for an internal member (null for a pending external invite).

fields.name: email
fields.docComment: Raw email for a pending/external invite (null once resolved to a member).

fields.name: name
fields.docComment:
Denormalized display name for the People-with-access list (the engine does
not own the user table; the web app refines this via useTenantMembers()).

fields.name: invitedById
fields.docComment: Clerk user id of the inviter (audit / "invited by").

models.name: WsNotification
models.docComment:
In-app notification (E-19). Targets a Clerk user id (recipientId) so the
notification bell can list a member's notifications across all drafts in the
tenant. Display fields are denormalized (the engine doesn't own the user
table). `actionable` is true only while a collab_invite is still pending.

models.name: WsDocument
models.docComment:
A document is one tab within a draft/packet. A simple draft has exactly one;
a packet has 2+ (cover letter, fact sheet, appendix, ...). (handoff §12.12)

fields.name: body
fields.docComment:
Rich document body: ordered blocks (sections, photo, table, logo).
Stored as JSONB so the editor's block model round-trips losslessly.

models.name: WsTemplate
models.docComment:
A reusable document structure (handoff Templates, §12.15). 2 per product
(primary + secondary) seeded globally; tenants may add their own later.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.docComment: GLOBAL templates have tenantId null; tenant-authored templates carry it.

fields.name: product
fields.docComment: exact work-product name string the template applies to (must match).

fields.name: elements
fields.docComment: subset of Photos · Tables · Logos · Cover letter · Budget exhibit · Charts

fields.name: sections
fields.docComment: ordered section names — seeds cfg.sections[] on apply.

models.name: WsComment
models.docComment:
In-editor comment (handoff §12.7). Anchored to a document range so the
highlight survives re-render. Threaded via parentId. Resolvable.

fields.name: authorId
fields.docComment: Clerk user id of the comment author (engine doesn't own the user table).

fields.name: quote
fields.docComment: Quoted text snapshot + serialized range anchor (start/end offsets, path).

models.name: WsDocVersion
models.docComment:
A point-in-time snapshot of a draft (Phase 6b version history). Created on a
manual "Save draft" (and restorable). `snapshot` carries the full draft config
+ each document body at save time so a restore is lossless. Tenant-scoped.

fields.name: label
fields.docComment: Human label ("Edited The ask", "Drafted Problem statement"). Optional.

fields.name: authorId
fields.docComment:
Clerk user id of the author (engine doesn't own the user table). For a
Meri-authored version this is the user who triggered the save.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.docComment:
Full draft state at save time: { docTitle, config, documents: [{id,name,
ordinal,body}], ask }.

models.name: WsEditLock
models.docComment:
Two-sided concurrent-edit lock (Phase 6b, Q-ED-2). One row per draft (draftId
is the PK). DB + polling, no websockets. The holder heartbeats while editing;
a viewer may `request` edit (the holder is notified) or `take over` once the
holder has been inactive (lastHeartbeatAt older than the inactivity window).
Tenant-scoped.

fields.name: draftId
fields.docComment: The draft this lock guards (one lock per draft).

fields.name: holderId
fields.docComment: Current holder (Clerk user id) + a denormalized display name for the banner.

fields.name: requestedById
fields.docComment: A pending "request to edit" from a viewer (cleared on take-over / release).

models.name: WsContextItem
models.docComment:
A piece of context attached to a draft for Meri grounding (handoff §12.16 +
Build Context). kind = source | news | free-text. Payload carries the item.

fields.name: payload
fields.docComment:
For news: { headline, source, date, url, relevantClients, relevantOffices }.
For source: { sourceType, refId, label }. For free-text: { text }.

models.name: WsIntake
models.docComment:
One row per intake request. The idempotency key (tenant + user + key) is
unique so a replay returns the same draftId/runId without new provider work.

fields.name: actorId
fields.docComment: Clerk user id of the requester.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.docComment: Caller-generated idempotency key (UUID recommended).

fields.name: draftId
fields.docComment: The draft created by this intake.

fields.name: runId
fields.docComment:
The durable generation run created by this intake. @unique: each run is
created by at most one intake (1-1).

fields.name: blueprintVersionId
fields.docComment: The blueprint version pinned at intake time.

fields.name: intakeSnapshot
fields.docComment: Immutable intake snapshot: goal, clientId, source IDs, context selections.

models.name: WsGenerationRun
models.docComment:
Durable generation run. The worker claims a lease, executes stages, and
updates per-section status. Survives browser reloads, ECS restarts, and
worker retries.

fields.name: actorId
fields.docComment: Clerk user id of the user who initiated the run.

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: Run status: queued | active | complete | partial | failed | cancelled

fields.name: stage
fields.docComment:
Current stage: queued | preflight | evidence_plan | narrative_plan |
  drafting | editorial_pass | assurance | snapshot | complete

fields.name: agentRevision
fields.docComment: Agent revision at run start (for optimistic concurrency on completion).

fields.name: leaseHolder
fields.docComment:
Lease holder (worker id) and lease expiry. Atomic claim: a worker
updates leaseHolder + leaseExpiresAt only if status is 'queued' or the
lease has expired.

fields.name: provider
fields.docComment: Provider telemetry (filled on completion).

fields.name: sectionStates
fields.docComment: Per-section status: { sectionId: { status, error, contentHash, citations } }

fields.name: stages
fields.docComment: Stage history: [{ name, status, startedAt, completedAt, detail }]

fields.name: errorMessage
fields.docComment: Run-level error message (for failed runs).

fields.name: settings
fields.docComment: Theme settings: { pageSize, margins, paperColor, fontFamilies, letterhead, ... }

models.name: WsBrandAsset
models.docComment: ── Brand Assets: firm logos and marks uploaded for theme letterheads (GAPS §16)

fields.name: objectKey
fields.docComment: S3 object key (the upload pipeline stores the object; we keep the key).

fields.name: filename
fields.docComment: Original filename for display.

fields.name: mimeType
fields.docComment: MIME type (image/png, image/svg+xml, etc.)

fields.name: sizeBytes
fields.docComment: Size in bytes.

fields.name: url
fields.docComment: Public-facing URL (presigned or CDN) for the asset.

fields.name: ownerId
fields.docComment: Clerk user id of the owner (same id-space as WsDraft.ownerId).

fields.name: clientId
fields.docComment: apps/api clients.id — the sponsoring client. No FK (cross-schema).

fields.name: resolutionStatus
fields.docComment: clean | partial | null (resolution not run yet)

fields.name: provenance
fields.docComment: As-generated provenance summary (source counts, corrections, model).

fields.name: firstPage
fields.docComment: User edits to the cover and schedule; independent of generated evidence.

fields.name: eventId
fields.docComment: apps/api meetings.id (the calendar event). No FK.

fields.name: event
fields.docComment: Calendar event snapshot as selected (subject, times, attendees, reason).

fields.name: resolution
fields.docComment: MeetingResolution — the chain plus user corrections (authoritative here).

fields.name: context
fields.docComment: MeetingContextRecord — { note, carry, threadIds }: what the user chose.

fields.name: section
fields.docComment: MeetingSection — Focus / Background, status and flags.

fields.name: sourceSet
fields.docComment: The source set actually assembled into the last prompt (provenance).

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: queued | running | complete | failed

fields.name: units
fields.docComment: [{ meetingId, state, sectionId, reason, at }]

fields.name: events
fields.docComment: Ordered SSE replay log: [{ seq, event, data }]

fields.name: status
fields.docComment: queued | ready | failed

fields.name: file
fields.docComment: Rendered bytes, kept so the signed URL serves exactly what was rendered.
